Clay Composite.hab: Thick grey and red clay beds along slow river bends and village brickfields, usually under a foot of topsoil where reeds grow and puddles never quite drain.
Clay Composite.how: Cut blocks with a flat spade, mix with sand and straw, then press and sun-dry for a week. Keep it damp under wet sacking until shaped or it cracks.

Copper.hab: Shallow seams in ordinary hillsides and stream cuts, easy to spot by green and blue staining on the rock and stunted grass growing above the vein.
Copper.how: A miner's pick, a shovel and half a day fill a sack with ore. Roast and smelt in a simple clay furnace; store ingots dry to slow the green crust.

Flax Fiber.hab: Grown in tilled farm fields with cool damp summers; tall slender stalks topped with small blue flowers that sway in rows by late summer.
Flax Fiber.how: Pull plants by the root, soak the stalks in a pond for two weeks, then beat and comb out the fibers. Store bundled and dry against mildew.

Flint.hab: Dark glassy nodules lying in chalk layers and tumbled in river gravels and quarry spoil, often with a white crust that hides the sharp black core.
Flint.how: Pry nodules loose with a pick or pick them from gravel by hand. Wear thick gloves; fresh breaks are razor sharp. Wrap in leather so they do not chip.

Hearthleaf.hab: Broad fuzzy leaves sprouting by cottage doors, hedgerows and kitchen gardens in any mild climate, thriving in soil enriched by hearth ash and kitchen scraps.
Hearthleaf.how: Pinch leaves off by hand in the morning, a basketful in minutes. Do not crush them until use or the bread scent fades; dry flat on cloth racks.

Herb Bundle.hab: Common kitchen and healing herbs that grow wild along lanes, field margins and forest clearings in temperate country, wherever sun and rain are both reliable.
Herb Bundle.how: Cut a mix of stems with a small knife, tie into bundles with twine, and hang upside down in a shaded airy loft for about a week to dry.

Lead.hab: Grey heavy galena veins in low-value hill mines, often beside limestone, where the rock is cubic and dull and nearby wells taste faintly sweet and wrong.
Lead.how: Break ore with a pick and hammer, then smelt in a well-vented furnace. Never breathe the fumes or eat with unwashed hands; store ingots wrapped in oilcloth.

Limestone.hab: Pale layered beds in hills, cliffs and valley walls, often full of tiny shell fossils, with springs and caves where water has eaten into the rock.
Limestone.how: Split blocks along bedding planes with wedges, hammers and pry bars. A quarry crew cuts a cartload a day; burn some in kilns for mortar lime.

Oak.hab: Broad, slow-growing trees across temperate forest regions and around logging camps, preferring deep loamy soil, with acorns and wide crowns marking mature stands.
Oak.how: Fell with axes and a two-man saw in winter when the sap is down, split into staves, then season under cover for several years before working.

Pyrite.hab: Brassy cubes scattered through dark shale seams and riverbed gravels in hill country, glinting gold in sunlight and often stinking of sulfur where wet.
Pyrite.how: Knock crystals out with a hammer and chisel or pick from gravel. Keep dry in a sealed jar; damp pyrite rots into crumbling acid powder.

Quarried Stone.hab: Plain sound bedrock exposed in hillsides and open quarry pits near most towns, chosen where the rock is free of cracks and rings when struck.
Quarried Stone.how: Drill a line of holes, drive iron wedges, and lever blocks free with crowbars. A crew needs a day per large block and an ox sled to haul.

Reed.hab: Dense tall stands in marshes, lake margins and slow river shallows, rooted in mud under knee-deep water, rustling loudly in any breeze.
Reed.how: Wade in and cut straight stems at the waterline with a sickle in autumn. Dry in bundles for a month; split or bent stems are useless for arrows.

Root Fiber.hab: Tough stringy roots of grasses and young trees in loose riverbank soil and eroded hillsides, where the earth has washed away to expose tangled mats.
Root Fiber.how: Dig with a trowel and pull roots gently to keep them long, then soak, strip the bark and twist into cord. Dry slowly to stay supple.

Rose Petal.hab: Wild briar roses in hedges and cultivated roses in manor gardens, blooming through early summer in sunny spots with rich, well-watered soil.
Rose Petal.how: Pluck petals by hand just after dawn dew dries, avoiding the thorns. Dry in shade on linen or press into oil the same day before they brown.

Slate.hab: Dark grey layered rock in quarries and riverbeds of old folded hills, splitting into thin even sheets, often with old roofs nearby built from it.
Slate.how: Lever out blocks, then split them with a broad chisel and mallet along the grain. Stack sheets upright on edge so they do not crack.

Sunpetal.hab: Small golden flowers in open sunny meadows, turning their faces to follow the sun all day and closing tight at dusk or under heavy cloud.
Sunpetal.how: Pick by hand only while the sun shines on them; flowers cut at night lose their holy warmth. Dry in sunlight and keep in a clear glass jar.

Tin.hab: Dark heavy cassiterite grains in shallow surface mines and stream gravels below granite hills, often found by panning heavy black sand from creek beds.
Tin.how: Dig and wash gravel in sluices, or pick ore from shallow pits, about a day per sack. Smelt with charcoal; store ingots warm, as cold tin crumbles.

Ash.hab: Tall straight trees in temperate forests and along damp valley floors, with pale grey bark, black winter buds and feathery compound leaves.
Ash.how: Fell young straight trunks in winter with axe and saw, rive into staves along the grain, and season under cover for at least a year.

Barrow Yarrow.hab: Feathery white-flowered yarrow growing thickly on old burial mounds and forgotten battlefields, rooted in soil once soaked with blood, blooming from midsummer to frost.
Barrow Yarrow.how: Cut stems with a knife and leave a coin or bow of respect, as barrow wardens notice thieves. Dry in bundles; bruised leaves work fresh on wounds.

Brass.hab: Rare yellow veins where copper and zinc lodes meet in old hill mines, usually smelted from mixed ore found beside pale calamine stone.
Brass.how: Mine the mixed ore with picks, then melt copper with calamine in sealed crucibles at a steady heat. The zinc fumes are poisonous; work in open air.

Bronze.hab: Not found in the ground; it is made in village and town forges wherever copper and tin trade routes meet, often near old river ports.
Bronze.how: Melt roughly nine parts copper to one part tin in a clay crucible and pour into stone moulds. A smith and an apprentice make a batch in a day.

Coral Fragment.hab: Broken branches of coral washed onto warm shallow reefs and tropical beaches after storms, piling in coves and tide pools beside shell and sea glass.
Coral Fragment.how: Gather at low tide in a basket, wearing sandals against sharp edges and urchins. Rinse in fresh water for a day and dry in shade so it does not bleach.

Crystal.hab: Clear crystal clusters lining hollow pockets in hillside caves and mine galleries, usually where mineral-rich water once seeped through cracked rock.
Crystal.how: Chisel clusters from the pocket wall with a small hammer, working slowly to avoid fractures. Wrap each piece in wool and carry in a padded box.

Granite.hab: Massive speckled grey and pink rock forming mountain cores, tors and cliff faces, often bare of soil and spotted with lichen.
Granite.how: Drill, wedge and split with iron tools, then dress with heavy hammers. Slow work: a mason crew cuts a block or two a day, and it is very heavy to haul.

Iron.hab: Red-brown and black ore veins in hill country and bog margins, betrayed by rusty streams, reddish soil and compasses that wander near the lode.
Iron.how: Dig ore with pick and shovel, roast it, then smelt in a charcoal bloomery for a full day. Store worked iron oiled and dry or it rusts.

Iron Ingot.hab: Produced at smelting towns and forges beside iron mines, where charcoal burners, water wheels and smoky bloomeries line the valley floor.
Iron Ingot.how: Smelt roasted ore into a bloom, hammer out the slag, and fold it into bars over two days. Stack ingots in a dry shed, lightly oiled.

Lodestone.hab: Black magnetic stone on iron-rich hilltops struck repeatedly by lightning, recognizable where nails jump toward it and compasses spin near the scorched rock.
Lodestone.how: Break pieces out with a bronze or wooden tool, since iron tools stick to it. Keep each piece apart in straw so it does not lose its pull.

Nickel.hab: Silvery green-stained ore found deep in older mines below ordinary iron seams, and occasionally in fallen star-iron craters on remote moors.
Nickel.how: Requires a deep shaft and several days of digging, then specialist smelting at high heat. The green ore dust irritates skin; work gloved and masked.

Nightshade.hab: Dark-leaved poisonous plants in shaded woods, damp ditches and the shadows of ruined walls, with drooping purple flowers and black berries.
Nightshade.how: Wear gloves and cut stems with a knife, never with bare hands. Dry separately from food herbs, label clearly, and keep in a sealed clay jar.

Quartz.hab: White and clear crystals in cave walls, hillside veins and stream gravels, often lining cracks in granite and glittering in shallow running water.
Quartz.how: Pick loose pieces from streams or tap crystals out with hammer and chisel. An afternoon yields a pouchful; wrap in cloth to protect points.

Raw Crystal Shard.hab: Rough unpolished crystal fragments scattered in mine spoil heaps, cave floors and freshly broken rock walls where larger crystal pockets once grew.
Raw Crystal Shard.how: Sift through rubble with a sieve and gloved hands, or chip shards from walls. Store wrapped in soft cloth inside a lined box to avoid cracks.

Salt Crystal.hab: Thick salt beds deep in old salt mines, and white crusts on coastal evaporation flats where seawater is trapped in shallow pans under hot sun.
Salt Crystal.how: Cut blocks in salt mines with picks and saws, or rake crusts from drying pans. Keep sealed in waxed sacks away from damp, which melts it.

Seasoaked Timber.hab: Old ship planks and driftwood logs soaked for years in salt water, found on rocky beaches, sunken wrecks in shallow bays and abandoned piers.
Seasoaked Timber.how: Haul out with ropes and a boat hook at low tide, then dry slowly under cover for months. Fast drying warps and splits the wood.

Silverleaf.hab: Low shrubs with silver-backed leaves along clear riverbanks, where roots reach the water and the leaves flash pale when the wind turns them.
Silverleaf.how: Pick upper leaves by hand at dawn, leaving roots and lower stems to regrow. Dry in shade within a day or the healing virtue fades.

Wolfsbane Root.hab: Purple-hooded flowers on shaded forest edges and damp clearings, often in hills where wolves and shapechangers roam, blooming in late summer.
Wolfsbane Root.how: Dig the root with a trowel while gloved; the sap numbs and poisons skin. Wash, slice and dry, then keep in a stoppered vial away from food.

Amber.hab: Golden lumps of fossil resin buried in layered sands and lignite beds beneath ancient forests, and washed up on cold northern beaches after storms.
Amber.how: Dig carefully with a wooden trowel through soft beds or comb beaches after storms. Avoid heat and harsh rubbing; store wrapped in soft cloth.

Bloodroot.hab: Red-rooted plants growing on old battlefields and in graveyards, thriving in soil where blood was spilled, flowering pale white with crimson sap.
Bloodroot.how: Dig root with a bone or silver trowel at dusk and seal in a stoppered jar. The bleeding sap stains skin for days; wear gloves.

Electrum.hab: Pale gold-silver nuggets and flakes in certain riverbeds and gravel terraces below old volcanic hills, sometimes in thin veins through quartz.
Electrum.how: Pan or sluice river gravel for days, or follow the vein with a small shaft. Keep away from iron tools, which sour its lightning charge.

Greystone.hab: Plain grey bedrock in common quarries everywhere, chosen from layers that show no veins, crystals or colour, the dullest stone a quarry offers.
Greystone.how: Cut with ordinary quarry tools: wedges, hammers and saws. Handle it without charms or enchanted tools, which leave a magical trace it should not carry.

Heartpine.hab: Old pine forests on sandy uplands where centuries-old trees build dense, resin-soaked red heartwood, sometimes found preserved in long-fallen trunks.
Heartpine.how: Fell old trees or split long-dead stumps with axe and wedge, then cut out the resin-rich core. Season for a year; keep away from open flame.

Marble.hab: Veined white, grey or green crystalline rock in deep quarries cut into hillsides, often below layers of limestone baked by ancient pressure.
Marble.how: Saw and wedge blocks with care to avoid hidden cracks, then lower on rollers. A skilled crew may spend several days freeing one fine block.

Nightshade Berry.hab: Glossy black berries on straggling vines that climb ruined walls and graveyard fences, ripening in late summer in shaded, undisturbed corners.
Nightshade Berry.how: Snip clusters with gloved hands into a lidded jar. Never touch eyes or mouth while picking; even the juice is deadly. Keep labeled and locked.

Obsidian.hab: Black glassy rock on the edges of cooled lava flows in volcanic regions and near fire plane borders, gleaming among ash and pumice.
Obsidian.how: Pick up fist-sized pieces or lever them from flow edges, wearing heavy gloves. Wrap each stone separately in leather; knocks shatter it.

Owlseye Moss.hab: Pale moss on the north faces of very old trees in damp shaded forests, its golden spore-heads glimmering like tiny eyes after dark.
Owlseye Moss.how: Scrape gently with a thin knife only at night, when the glow shows the best patches. Store in a dark tin; daylight dims the spores.

Rose Gold.hab: Pinkish gold flakes and small nuggets in placer gravels at the foot of copper-rich hills, settling in bends where streams slow down.
Rose Gold.how: Pan or sluice gravel for days with pan, shovel and patience. Pick out pink flakes by hand and store in a corked quill or small vial.

Tungsten Ore.hab: Heavy dark ore in deep granite veins beside tin lodes, often found only after miners follow a tin seam far into the hill.
Tungsten Ore.how: Dig deep with hardened picks over several days. It is heavy and splinters when struck; protect eyes. Ordinary forges cannot melt it.

Yew.hab: Ancient dark-needled trees in old forests, churchyards and sacred groves, often hundreds of years old, with red berries and hollow trunks.
Yew.how: Cut a single stave with permission or a respectful offering, keeping heartwood and sapwood together. Season for two years; leaves and seeds are poisonous.

Amethyst.hab: Purple crystal geodes deep in crystal caves and in volcanic rock pockets near places where minds feel clearer, sometimes buzzing with faint psychic hum.
Amethyst.how: Crack geodes with a chisel and hammer, then work clusters free over hours. Store wrapped; sunlight fades the colour. Clear your mind first or headaches follow.

Ashwood.hab: Charred black trees in volcanic forests near fire plane borders, rooted in warm ash soil, with smoke rising from cracks in their bark.
Ashwood.how: Fell with fireproof gloves and a steel saw, quenching cuts with water. The red heartwood smolders for hours; store in stone sheds, never with dry tinder.

Deep Iron.hab: Dense dark iron ore far below common iron seams, in deep mines where the rock grows warm, the air thins and water drips constantly.
Deep Iron.how: A deep shaft and several days of shifts with heavy picks. Risk of cave-in and bad air; carry a caged songbird. Smelt in a hotter forge than usual.

Garnet.hab: Deep red crystals studded through iron-rich ore veins and dark schist in old mining hills, glinting like drops of blood in the rock face.
Garnet.how: Chip out crystals with a fine chisel while mining iron, over a day or two. Sort by colour; store in a felt-lined box to protect faces.

Gold.hab: Bright veins deep in quartz rock and loose nuggets in river gravels downstream of mountains, often guarded by claim holders or local lords.
Gold.how: Dig deep mine galleries or pan rivers for days. Crush ore and wash with water; avoid the old quicksilver method in closed rooms. Guard the take well.

Ironbark Resin.hab: Amber sap that wells from wounds in ironbark trees in ancient oak forests, hardening into horn-like lumps on the bark over several weeks.
Ironbark Resin.how: Cut a shallow notch with a steel knife and return a month later to pry off hardened resin. Melt slowly in a double pot; overheating ruins it.

Obsidian Glass.hab: Fresh volcanic glass formed where lava hit water or air quickly, found on recent flows, crater rims and shorelines after eruptions.
Obsidian Glass.how: Collect soon after an eruption, wearing boots and gloves against heat and edges. Avoid still-warm flows. Wrap each piece in thick cloth.

Onyx.hab: Black banded stone in bedrock beneath old burial grounds and near shadow-touched places, cold to the touch and often in layers under crypt floors.
Onyx.how: Dig carefully beneath burial sites, ideally with priestly permission; disturbed dead may rise. Chisel out bands and wrap in black cloth.

Quicksilver.hab: Liquid silver beads in red cinnabar deposits, collecting in hollows of mine floors where the rock is soft, warm and bright red.
Quicksilver.how: Mine the cinnabar and roast it under a glass hood, catching droplets. Fumes are deadly; work outdoors, masked. Store in sealed iron flasks.

River Pearl.hab: Inside freshwater mussels on clean gravel beds of cool rivers, in slow deep pools where shell beds line the bottom.
River Pearl.how: Wade or dive and open mussels with a thin knife; most hold nothing. A good day yields one or two pearls. Store in soft cloth, away from acid.

Sleepwort.hab: Drooping blue bells in damp meadows near streams and fog-filled hollows, flowering in late spring and swaying gently even in still air.
Sleepwort.how: Pick with gloves and a cloth over the nose; the pollen makes collectors drowsy. Dry in a ventilated shed and store in a sealed jar.

Spiderstone.hab: Dark gem nodules in caves thick with webs of magical giant spiders, embedded in walls coated with silk and the remains of their prey.
Spiderstone.how: Clear webs with fire or blades, then chisel stones out quickly before the spiders return. Bring antivenom and armed guards; store in sealed boxes.

Steel.hab: Not found in nature; made in master forges in towns with good iron and charcoal, where skilled smiths guard their carbon recipes closely.
Steel.how: Heat iron with carbon in a crucible or fold it with charcoal under the hammer for days. Quench carefully; store oiled to stop rust.

Thornwood.hab: Gnarled calcified thorn trees in ancient thorn forests where centuries have hardened the wood to stone, thickets thick enough to stop horses.
Thornwood.how: Cut a path with heavy blades and armour, then saw branches with care to keep the thorns. Takes a full day and torn skin; carry in leather wraps.

Topaz.hab: Golden and blue crystals in granite pockets near mountain peaks often struck by lightning, the rock scorched and faintly humming before storms.
Topaz.how: Climb high and chisel out crystals from pockets during calm weather; storms bring lightning. Use rubber gloves and store in wool-wrapped glass.

White Gold.hab: Pale gold veins in quartz reefs high in cold northern mountains, where nickel stains the rock and snow lies most of the year.
White Gold.how: Mine reefs with picks through short summers, crushing quartz to free the gold. Several weeks of work for a small pouch; cold kills the careless.

Aquamarine.hab: Sea-blue crystals in wind-swept sea cliffs and rocky shorelines, lodged in pale pegmatite seams that face the open ocean.
Aquamarine.how: Rope down cliffs on calm days and chisel crystals out by hand. High winds and slick rock are deadly. Wrap gems in sailcloth.

Blackthorn.hab: Dense spiny hedges along old boundaries, field edges and cursed groves where the land between worlds feels thin and mist lingers at dusk.
Blackthorn.how: Cut stout stems in winter with a hooked knife and thick gloves, leaving an offering for the hedge spirits. Season for a year by the hearth.

Cobalt.hab: Silvery ore with pink-blue staining deep in old mines, often in arsenic-tainted rock where miners suffer coughs and dying canaries.
Cobalt.how: Dig deep with picks and roast the ore carefully; the fumes carry poison. Work masked, and wash well. Smelting takes skilled hands and several days.

Damascus Steel.hab: Not mined; folded at master forges in old trade cities, where smiths keep layered billets of hard and soft iron in locked guild halls.
Damascus Steel.how: Forge-weld and fold bars dozens of times over weeks, then etch to reveal the pattern. Requires a master smith's skill and costly fuel.

Ebonwood.hab: Jet-black hardwood trees deep in shadow-touched jungles, where sunlight barely reaches the floor and strange beasts hunt in the dim green.
Ebonwood.how: Requires an expedition of weeks and steel saws; the wood blunts axes. Guard against jungle predators. Float logs downriver with care; they sink.

Ironwood.hab: Rare, dense trees in remote old-growth forests and deep wilderness, often far from roads and recognized by grey bark that rings like metal when struck.
Ironwood.how: Saw with hardened blades over two or three days per trunk; axes chip. Too heavy to float; haul by ox team. Season slowly for a year.

Jade.hab: Green boulders and veins in eastern mountains and spirit-touched rivers, often hidden beneath plain brown rinds that must be cut to show the colour.
Jade.how: Cut slowly with sand and wire saws, as hammers bruise it. Gifts to local river spirits are wise. Work takes days; store in silk.

Kingsbane Mushroom.hab: Pale violet mushrooms growing in the deepest rot of old forests, on fallen trunks and in dark hollows, mostly after long autumn rains.
Kingsbane Mushroom.how: Cut with gloves and a covered face; spores poison through skin and breath. Carry in sealed glass jars; never store near food or wine.

Moonstone.hab: Pale milky stones in coastal rock beds and moonlit beaches, shining faintly at night, most visible during the full moon after high tides.
Moonstone.how: Dig and search only under full moonlight when the stones glow; by day they look like plain pebbles. Store in dark velvet away from sunlight.

Obsidian Gem.hab: Black glossy gems formed in volcanic sites where shadow and fire meet, lodged in old lava tubes near Shadowfell borders, cold despite the heat.
Obsidian Gem.how: Enter lava tubes with light and heat protection, then chisel gems free over hours. Shadows thicken around collectors; carry bright lanterns and a guide.

Peridot.hab: Lime-green crystals in black basalt on volcanic islands and near Abyssal plane borders, often in hot sulfurous fields where demons have walked.
Peridot.how: Chip crystals from basalt with heat-resistant tools, wearing masks against fumes. Demonic presences may linger; bring protection and leave fast.

Silver.hab: Bright veins with lead and copper in deep silver mines, sometimes in thin wiry threads through quartz and dark sulfide rock.
Silver.how: Mine deep with picks and refine by heating with lead over days. Hold the work under guard; silver mines attract thieves. Polish and wrap in cloth.

Tidecoral.hab: Blue coral forests in deep sea currents and the Plane of Water, growing on rocks swept by strong, cold underwater rivers far from shore.
Tidecoral.how: Dive with water-breathing magic and cut branches with a coral saw. Strong currents drag divers away. Keep it wet in sealed seawater tanks.

Wootz Steel.hab: Not mined; made in sealed clay crucibles in hot southern desert kingdoms, where furnace masters keep their charcoal and ore recipes secret.
Wootz Steel.how: Melt iron with plant matter in sealed crucibles for days, then cool slowly into cakes. Work only at low heat or the pattern is lost.

Blackiron.hab: Dense black ore in volcanic mines where heat rises from below, often near lava tunnels and steaming vents deep under smoking mountains.
Blackiron.how: Dig in short shifts in thick leathers due to heat, about a week per load. Bad air and lava seepage kill; smelt in an extra-hot forge.

Bloodstone.hab: Dark green stone spotted red in rock beneath old battlefields and cursed earth, where soil is iron-stained and grass grows thin and dark.
Bloodstone.how: Dig through soaked battlefield ground with spades over days. Restless spirits may stir; bring a cleric. Store stones in iron-banded boxes.

Coldstone.hab: Frost-white stone in the deepest arctic caverns, far beneath ice sheets, where breath freezes instantly and walls glitter with permanent rime.
Coldstone.how: Requires furs, fire magic and a week-long descent. Handle only with thick padded tongs; bare skin freezes to it. Store in insulated chests.

Crownmallow.hab: Tall purple mallow grown in palace gardens and monastery cloisters, rarely wild, often under the eye of gardeners, guards or monks.
Crownmallow.how: Obtain by trade, favour or careful theft; dig roots in autumn with a trowel. Dry slowly and keep sealed; royal gardens are heavily guarded.

Dark-heart Oak.hab: Ancient oaks in deep shadowed groves whose cores have turned black with age and shadow, where light fades early and birdsong is rare.
Dark-heart Oak.how: Fell with steel axes over two days and cut out the black heartwood. Ward the camp; shadows in the grove resent the harvest. Season a year.

Deepstone.hab: Extremely dense dark stone deep in the underdark and Plane of Earth borders, under crushing pressure far below common mines.
Deepstone.how: Reach by deep descent with guides and strong lamps. Takes many days with hardened tools; ordinary picks break. Heavy beasts and cave-ins threaten.

Emerald.hab: Rich green crystals in deep jungle mines and near fey borders, embedded in dark shale where plants grow unusually lush above.
Emerald.how: Dig slowly with small chisels in hot, damp galleries over weeks. Emeralds crack easily; oil and wrap in silk. Fey may claim payment.

Ironbark.hab: Bark of ancient oaks in places of strong natural magic, hardened like iron, often in groves guarded by druids or tree spirits.
Ironbark.how: Peel in sheets with steel tools only after asking the grove's guardians; theft angers druids. Takes a day per tree and leaves it alive.

Platinum.hab: Silver-white grains in rare deep veins and dark river sands, often below old volcanic intrusions far from settled lands.
Platinum.how: Mine deep shafts or wash sands for weeks, collecting tiny grains. Extremely hard to melt; needs a specialist forge. Store in locked boxes.

Ruby.hab: Deep red crystals in marble and basalt beneath volcanic regions and deep mines, warm to the touch and glowing faintly in torchlight.
Ruby.how: Dig deep in hot galleries over weeks, chiselling gently to avoid cracks. Heat sickness and lava risk; store gems in cool cloth bags.

Sapphire.hab: Blue crystals in deep water-fed deposits and mountain mines, often where cold underground streams cool the rock and frost forms on clustered stones.
Sapphire.how: Dig deep or pump out flooded galleries, then chisel gems free over weeks. Keep clustered stones apart; they chill and crack each other.

Tamahagane.hab: Black iron sand on coastal beaches and river deltas, gathered in dark streaks after storms and smelted in clay furnaces nearby.
Tamahagane.how: Wash sand in channels, then smelt in a clay furnace for three days and nights without rest. Break it open and sort pieces by hand.

Titanium.hab: Dark gleaming ore in deep veins and volcanic regions, often in black sand and stone beside old lava flows far underground.
Titanium.how: Mine deep and smelt at extreme temperatures with specialist methods; ordinary forges fail. Takes weeks per batch; molten metal ignites easily.

Adaptation Stone.hab: Dull green pebbles in deep veins beneath Human riverbeds where the Adaptation Rune's power pools, shifting colour to match the surrounding mud and stone.
Adaptation Stone.how: Dig deep below the riverbed and test stones by placing them on cloth; true ones change colour within days. Store in plain clay pots.

Alchemist's Gold.hab: Not found in nature; made in alchemical labs and hidden workshops, often by forgers and testers working with secret recipes and strange reagents.
Alchemist's Gold.how: Synthesize over days from costly reagents and skilled alchemy. Store separately from real gold and label it, since only Detect Magic tells them apart.

Alchemy Stone.hab: Mottled orange and violet stones in deep veins near salt flats and beneath old brewers' cellars, where the Alchemy Rune's power pools and water fizzes.
Alchemy Stone.how: Dig deep veins with picks over days, keeping stones dry, as they fizz and dissolve when wet. Store in waxed boxes away from potions.

Alexandrite.hab: Colour-shifting crystals in veins near shifting magical nexuses, where light seems to bend and stones change hue between red and green.
Alexandrite.how: Dig cautiously; the nexus warps magic and random surges strike collectors. Chisel slowly and store in lead boxes to calm their shifts.

Ambulance Stone.hab: Soft white stones with red cross-grain in deep veins beneath old Human battlefields, where wounded soldiers were dragged to safety.
Ambulance Stone.how: Dig beneath field hospitals of old battles over several days, with respect for the dead. Store wrapped in clean bandage linen.

Angerstone.hab: Rough red stones in quarry veins where old feuds were fought and the Anger Rune's power pools, warming when insults are spoken nearby.
Angerstone.how: Mine in calm, quiet crews; arguments make the stones hot enough to burn. Chisel out over days and store in cool water-filled jars.

Aptitude Stone.hab: Small amber stones with inner sparks in deep veins below creek beds near old schools and training yards, where the Aptitude Rune's power pools.
Aptitude Stone.how: Dig carefully below the creek over several days. Stones brighten when held by learners; test this way. Store in soft cloth bags.

Ascendstone.hab: Light cloudy white stones in veins beneath Human hilltops and old tower foundations, where the Ascend Rune's power pools and dust floats upward.
Ascendstone.how: Dig deep below hilltops and catch stones in a net as they drift upward when freed. Store in weighted iron cages or they float away.

Axestone.hab: Heavy grey wedge-shaped stones in veins under forests where woodcutters work, often beneath fallen trees where the Axe Rune's power pools.
Axestone.how: Dig beneath old fallen trunks with pick and shovel over days. Their natural edges cut skin; wear gloves and wrap them in thick leather.

Blossomstone.hab: Soft pink stones with petal flakes in veins beneath orchards and riverbanks under flowering trees, where the Blossom Rune's power pools.
Blossomstone.how: Dig gently in spring under flowering trees, a few days for a handful. Avoid harsh tools that crush petal flakes. Store in silk pouches.

Cagestone.hab: Stones with crisscrossed ridges like bars, found deep in mine veins where crystals grow in tight lattices and the Cage Rune's power pools.
Cagestone.how: Chisel out whole lattice blocks carefully over days; miners who linger too long feel trapped. Store in open baskets, never sealed boxes.

Chainstone.hab: Heavy grey stones of interlocking rings in veins beneath old prison quarries where shackles were forged and the Chain Rune's power pools.
Chainstone.how: Dig deep in prison quarries over several days, freeing the stone without breaking rings. Heavy; carry on sledges. Store chained or bound.

Charmstone.hab: Small eye-catching pink stones in veins under river shallows where travelers pause, the Charm Rune's power pooling beneath the gravel.
Charmstone.how: Dig below the gravel over a few days, working blindfolded at times, as the stones lure people to pocket them. Store in dark boxes.

Chemical Stone.hab: Banded yellow, green and blue stones in deep veins beneath old alchemical pits, where the Chemical Rune's power pools and the soil stinks.
Chemical Stone.how: Dig in dry weather wearing masks; wet stones smoke with harmful fumes. Takes days. Store sealed in glass jars, labeled and dry.

Choicestone.hab: Two-coloured stones in veins beneath old crossroads where paths split and the Choice Rune's power pools, each half a different hue.
Choicestone.how: Dig beneath crossroads over several days, choosing a direction and sticking to it, as hesitation makes stones crumble. Store in paired pouches.

Cleanstone.hab: Smooth white stones in veins beneath cold clear streams, where the Clean Rune's power pools and no moss or silt clings to the rocks.
Cleanstone.how: Dig below the streambed in cold water over days, keeping hands clean, as dirt makes the stones slip. Store in clean linen.

Crawling Hand Stone.hab: Knuckled pink pebbles shaped like curled fingers in veins under old graveyards and battlefields, where the Crawling Hand Rune's power pools.
Crawling Hand Stone.how: Dig at night with a cleric present; stones twitch and crawl when freed. Grab with tongs and store in locked iron boxes.

Disablestone.hab: Small grey stones with a numbing chill in veins beneath shallow riverbeds and fields, where the Disable Rune's power pools.
Disablestone.how: Dig over a few days with gloves; bare hands go numb for hours. Use tongs and store in fur-lined boxes so the chill does not spread.

Dragonblood Pepper.hab: Scarlet pepper bushes on hot volcanic hillsides, rooted in black ash soil said to be soaked with old dragon blood, ripening in high summer.
Dragonblood Pepper.how: Pick with thick gloves and covered eyes; the juice blisters skin. Dry on stone racks in the sun and store in sealed clay jars.

Dwarf-Steel.hab: Not mined directly; smelted in clan forge-halls under the highest peaks, using ore and secret fluxes guarded by mountain clans.
Dwarf-Steel.how: Earned through trade, favour or alliance with a clan; outsiders rarely see the forge. Smelting takes weeks; store oiled in wool.

Efficiencystone.hab: Neatly squared grey stones in veins beneath old quarries and workshops, where the Efficiency Rune's power pools and tools never seem to go missing.
Efficiencystone.how: Dig with well-planned shafts; wasted effort makes stones crack. A tidy crew takes days. Store stacked in neat rows in wooden crates.

Electricstone.hab: Small yellow sparking stones in veins under storm-struck hills where the Electric Rune's power pools and hair stands up on the slope.
Electricstone.how: Dig with wooden or rubber tools only, as metal draws shocks. Work outside storms. Store in glass jars lined with wool.

Envystone.hab: Dull green stones in veins beneath mines and market towns, where the Envy Rune's power pools and the stones glow brighter near wealth.
Envystone.how: Dig over several days in teams that trust each other, as quarrels break out. Store in plain boxes away from coins and gems.

Fatestone.hab: Small stones with fine woven threads inside, in veins beneath caves and old temples where the Fate Rune's power pools and echoes sound like whispers.
Fatestone.how: Dig slowly over days without forcing; stones resist the unworthy and break. Store wrapped in thread and never sell one cheaply.

Fatiguestone.hab: Heavy grey sleepy stones in veins beneath worn hills where the Fatigue Rune's power pools and travelers feel tired for no reason.
Fatiguestone.how: Dig in short shifts with rested crews; long contact drains strength. Takes days. Store in sealed lead-lined boxes to block the weariness.

Flowerstone.hab: Small pink and cream petal-patterned stones in veins beneath meadows and garden beds, where the Flower Rune's power pools and smells sweet.
Flowerstone.how: Dig gently in spring over several days, keeping the soil intact. Rough tools crush the patterns. Store in soft cloth with dried petals.

Foreststone.hab: Mossy green stones with root-like brown streaks in veins under old trees in woodland, where the Forest Rune's power pools.
Foreststone.how: Dig between roots carefully over days without killing trees; angry forest spirits stir. Store damp in moss-lined boxes.

Gamblestone.hab: Speckled stones dotted with pips like dice in veins beneath river gravel near old trading towns, where the Gamble Rune's power pools.
Gamblestone.how: Dig over days and roll each stone; only true ones land differently every throw. Store in pouches and keep away from gamblers.

Giftstone.hab: Smooth rosy stones with a golden glow in veins beneath shrines where strangers leave offerings and the Gift Rune's power pools.
Giftstone.how: Dig with the shrine keeper's blessing and leave an offering in return, or stones vanish. Takes days. Store in gift boxes, never sold.

Glacial Iron.hab: Cold iron in veins under glaciers on frozen mountain peaks and Plane of Ice borders, where centuries of crushing ice formed it.
Glacial Iron.how: Requires mountaineering, furs and fire magic. Chip through ice and rock for days; bare skin freezes to the ore. Store in insulated chests.

Gnomestone.hab: Rough brown stones threaded with root fibers in veins deep in old soil, smelling of fresh earth where the Gnome Rune's power pools.
Gnomestone.how: Dig deep in fertile land over days, leaving the topsoil intact for crops. Burrowing creatures guard veins. Store in earth-filled sacks.

Hatestone.hab: Cold black-red stones in veins beneath ruins where old feuds burned out and the Hate Rune's power pools, heavy and unsettling to hold.
Hatestone.how: Dig over several days with calm crews and a cleric; stones stir resentment. Store separately in iron boxes away from allies.

Heartbreakstone.hab: Rose-coloured stones split in two in veins beneath streams near abandoned homes, where the Heartbreak Rune's power pools.
Heartbreakstone.how: Dig over days and collect both halves together; one half alone loses power. Holders feel grief; store the pairs in separate pouches.

Hurtstone.hab: Plain rough grey stones in veins under fields where many fights broke out and the Hurt Rune's power pools, painful to grip hard.
Hurtstone.how: Dig over days with padded gloves and loose grips; squeezing hurts. Store in padded sacks and keep away from tempers.

Illusionstone.hab: Shimmering shadowless stones in veins beneath caves full of false echoes, where the Illusion Rune's power pools and passages seem to move.
Illusionstone.how: Dig over days with a rope guide; false tunnels mislead miners. Test stones for shadows by lamp. Store in dark cloth bags.

Imagestone.hab: Flat glossy black stones in veins beneath still pools and river shallows, where the Image Rune's power pools and reflections linger.
Imagestone.how: Dig below the pool over days, covering stones at once so they capture nothing unwanted. Store wrapped in black cloth.

Instigatestone.hab: Spiky red-orange stones in veins beneath markets and taverns where the Instigate Rune's power pools and arguments break out often.
Instigatestone.how: Dig in silence and short shifts; stones heat with every quarrel. Takes days. Store in cool sand-filled boxes away from crowds.

Lavastone.hab: Heavy black rocks with glowing orange cracks in veins near Human volcanoes, where the Lava Rune's power pools and the ground stays warm.
Lavastone.how: Dig in heat-resistant gear with stone tools; metal softens near it. Takes days near danger. Store in stone boxes, never in wood.

Leechstone.hab: Dark red pitted stones in veins beneath battlefield soil where the Lifesteal Rune's power pools, warming near the wounded.
Leechstone.how: Dig over days without open wounds; stones drain blood through cuts. Use tongs and store in sealed glass jars.

Liestone.hab: Small stones looking different to each viewer, in veins beneath marketplaces and back alleys where the Lies Rune's power pools.
Liestone.how: Dig with a trusted crew over days, testing stones with truth magic, as fakes abound. Store in labeled locked boxes with written records.

Luststone.hab: Smooth warm crimson stones in veins beneath riverbeds where the Lust Rune's power pools and collectors feel a pull to hold them.
Luststone.how: Dig over days and handle with gloves; bare skin makes them hard to let go. Store in locked boxes with a trusted keeper.

Martial Spirit Stone.hab: Warm ivory stones in veins beneath monasteries and old martial dojos, where the Martial Spirit Rune's power pools and training never stops.
Martial Spirit Stone.how: Dig with the masters' consent after proving discipline, often over weeks. Stones glow for true trainees. Store wrapped in a training sash.

Microstone.hab: Sand-sized stones in veins beneath river silt where the Micro Rune's power pools, invisible without a lens among ordinary grains.
Microstone.how: Dig silt and sift with fine mesh and a lens over days. Collect with tweezers into a sealed glass vial; a sneeze loses them.

Mirrorstone.hab: Thin glassy silver stones in veins beneath still ponds and polished cliffs that catch the morning sun, where the Reflection Rune's power pools.
Mirrorstone.how: Dig and pry stones free at dawn when they shine brightest. They crack easily; wrap each in soft velvet and store flat.

Multiplystone.hab: Small stones always found in pairs in cave veins where the Multiply Rune's power pools, their numbers shifting when counted.
Multiplystone.how: Dig over days and take stones in pairs; lone ones fade. Count once only and record it. Store in paired pouches.

Naturestone.hab: Mossy green stones streaked brown and blue in forest veins, where the Nature Rune's power pools and small plants sprout around them.
Naturestone.how: Dig carefully around roots over days, replanting what you disturb. Store in damp moss-lined boxes where they keep sprouting.

Omenstone.hab: Black and white stones in veins beneath crossroads where the Omen Rune's power pools, their patterns shifting into warning shapes.
Omenstone.how: Dig over days, watching patterns for danger signs, and stop if warnings appear. Store in sealed boxes and check them daily.

Organicstone.hab: Spongy green living stones in moist veins of the Human realm where the Organic Rune's power pools, growing roots toward water.
Organicstone.how: Dig over days and lift stones with their roots intact. Keep damp in clay pots with water; dry stones die.

Parasite Stone.hab: Pale clinging stones in veins of the Human realm where the Parasitism Rune's power pools, sticking to rock and draining warmth from it.
Parasite Stone.how: Dig over days with thick gloves; stones stick to skin and drain warmth. Pry off with wooden tools and store in iron boxes.

Probability Stone.hab: Pale grey dotted pebbles in veins below riverbeds near gambling towns and crossroads, where the Probability Rune's power pools.
Probability Stone.how: Dig over days and check dots shift when looked at again. Luck turns odd near them; store in plain pouches and avoid gambling.

Rerollstone.hab: Cube-shaped grey stones with faint pips in veins beneath creek gravel near gaming houses and dice tables, where the Reroll Rune's power pools.
Rerollstone.how: Dig over days and test by rolling; true stones never land the same twice. Store in dice bags away from gamblers.

Resistance Stone.hab: Dull brown stones in quarry veins where the Resistance Rune's power pools, denting under hammer blows but never cracking.
Resistance Stone.how: Dig over days with patience; hammers bounce off, so lever them out with pry bars. Store in ordinary sacks; they are hard to harm.

Reversestone.hab: Spiral stones in cave veins where dripping water climbs upward and the Reverse Rune's power pools, turning against any spin.
Reversestone.how: Dig over days, moving opposite to instinct, as stones push back. Store upside down in boxes with labels reversed.

Ridingstone.hab: Grey and white wind-streaked stones in veins beneath horse plains and old caravan roads, where the Riding Rune's power pools.
Ridingstone.how: Dig beneath old roads over days, ideally with horses nearby, as stones respond to them. Store in saddlebags lined with felt.

Scanstone.hab: Clear stones with sweeping rings of light in veins beneath watchtower foundations and border guard posts, where the Scan Rune's power pools.
Scanstone.how: Dig over days with the garrison's permission. Stones reveal hidden things when held; store in dark cases to stop their sweeping light.

Scentstone.hab: Porous tan stones in veins beneath forest game trails and hunting lodges, where the Scent Rune's power pools and smells linger.
Scentstone.how: Dig over days and keep stones away from strong odors, which soak in and ruin them. Store in sealed jars of clean air.

Scythestone.hab: Crescent grey stones with sharp edges in veins beneath farm fields after harvest and old smithies, where the Scythe Rune's power pools.
Scythestone.how: Dig after harvest over days with gloves; inner edges cut deep. Store wrapped in leather sheaths.

Seastone.hab: Blue-green stone on coastal cliffs shaped by the sea over millennia, exposed at low tide on wave-carved ledges and sea caves.
Seastone.how: Chisel from cliffs at low tide with ropes and anchors; high waves drown the careless. Keep stones wet in sealed seawater jars.

Shifterstone.hab: Colour-shifting stones in veins beneath marshes where the Shape-shifter Rune's power pools and nothing looks quite the same twice.
Shifterstone.how: Dig over days and mark stones with chalk; they blend into anything. Store in white boxes so they cannot hide.

Spatialstone.hab: Clear stones with folded space inside, in cave veins with odd echoes where the Spatial Rune's power pools and distances feel wrong.
Spatialstone.how: Dig carefully over days with rope lines; space bends and miners get lost. Store in lead-lined boxes to keep space steady.

Specterstone.hab: Cold blue veins under haunted ruins and old battlefields, where the Specter Rune pools in bedrock. Lamps gutter and breath fogs above a seam; it only shows its glow after midnight.
Specterstone.how: Dig down after midnight with a pick and chisel, working by candle. Ghosts drawn to the vein may follow the miner home; wrap each stone in grave linen and salt.

Splitstone.hab: Paired seams in lightning-split cliffs and beneath old dagger smithies, where the Split Rune pools in the bedrock. Look for rock fractured into two mirror faces along a straight line.
Splitstone.how: Chisel out both halves together over a long day; a stone taken without its twin goes dull. Bind the pair with wire and store them in one padded box.

Starfall Copper.hab: Blue-tinted copper inside meteorites that punched through several planes before landing, buried in glassy craters on remote moors and hills. Compasses twitch and grass grows stunted around the impact site.
Starfall Copper.how: Dig out the meteorite with picks and levers, then crack it open and smelt the copper apart from the stony crust. Takes several days and a hot crucible.

Tamestone.hab: Shallow brown veins beneath old herding trails, drove roads and stockyards, where generations of tamed beasts fed the Tame Rune. Animals grow calm and docile near the seam.
Tamestone.how: Dig it with a trowel and pick in half a day, bare-handed at the last; a stone struck by a whip or prod loses its warmth. Keep in soft leather.

Techstone.hab: Grooved grey veins in old mine workings and under long-used forges, where the Technology Rune pools in the bedrock. Tools left nearby tick, whir or tighten on their own.
Techstone.how: Cut it out with a miner's pick and fine chisels so the grooves are not broken, a day's careful work. Stored in oiled cloth, away from rust and water.

Time Duration Stone.hab: Hourglass-shaped nodules in bedrock beneath old sundials, clock towers and abbey bell houses, where the Time Duration Rune pools. Shadows on the dial slow or stall above a vein.
Time Duration Stone.how: Mine slowly with a pick and soft brush, never inverting the stone or its inner sand settles for good. Carry it upright in a wooden case; the work takes a day.

Transform Stone.hab: Restless veins under shifting soil, landslips and flood plains, where the Transformation Rune pools in bedrock. The ground above never looks the same two mornings running.
Transform Stone.how: One miner must keep eyes on the stone the whole time, or it changes shape and slips from the vein. Dig with a pick in a day; store in a lidded mirror box.

Truststone.hab: Clear white veins in bedrock beneath old wedding chapels, oath stones and treaty grounds, where the Trust Rune pools. A faint glow rises when two people stand together over a seam.
Truststone.how: Two workers who trust each other must dig it together with picks and lift it out jointly. A lie spoken while mining cracks it; wrap in clean white linen.

Twiststone.hab: Corkscrew veins in the bedrock of narrow rocky ravines, where the Twist Rune pools and strata bend into spirals. Paths and streams nearby wind more than they should.
Twiststone.how: Turn it out of the rock with a spiral auger and leather gloves, since the edges cut deep. A day's work; keep each stone in a padded box so it cannot snag.

Typhoonstone.hab: Grey-blue spiral veins in sea cliffs and coastal bedrock, where the Typhoon Rune pools. Fresh faces are bared only after the greatest storms tear away the rock and shingle.
Typhoonstone.how: Mine it from cliff tunnels in the calm days after a great storm, using pick and rope. It keeps misting; store sealed in waxed, salt-packed crates.

Unknownstone.hab: Lightless veins beneath places that no map records and no traveller remembers, where the Unknown Rune pools in bedrock. Surveyors lose count and directions blur near a seam.
Unknownstone.how: Finding the vein is the hard part; dig blind with a pick and string line to mark the way out. Never record its location or the stone fades. Wrap in black cloth.

Zephyr Stone.hab: Pale green veins under gentle hills and summer meadows, where the Zephyrus Rune pools in bedrock. A warm breeze rises from the ground even on still days.
Zephyr Stone.how: Dig it in summer with a spade and pick, about half a day. Kept in a closed jar it holds its breeze; left open, the wind slowly drains away.

Diamond.hab: Deep volcanic pipes far below the surface and rare celestial ore seams, where crushing pressure turns carbon to clear crystal. Blue clay and faint radiance mark a rich pipe.
Diamond.how: Requires a deep shaft, crews and weeks of digging through hard blue rock with steel picks. Wash and sort by hand; guard the finds against theft and store in locked boxes.

Elder Mandrake Root.hab: Grows on gallows hills where hanged men dripped onto the soil, rooting for a century before ripening. The leaves only show above ground under the full moon.
Elder Mandrake Root.how: Plug your ears with wax and tie a dog or rope to the stalk, pulling from a distance at full moon. Its scream can stop a heart. Store in a lidded clay pot.

Fathomstone.hab: Black crystal clusters on the walls of the deepest ocean trenches, in freezing dark water under crushing pressure. Only found where no light has ever reached.
Fathomstone.how: Needs water-breathing magic, a weighted diving bell or a sea-beast guide, plus hours of work with a hammer at depth. Keep it wet in sealed jars or it clouds.

Magmaite.hab: Forms deep in volcanic cores and in the burning rock of the Plane of Fire, where molten stone cools slowly into metal. Glowing cracks and choking fumes mark a seam.
Magmaite.how: Dig toward the volcanic core with fire-resistant gear and iron tongs; it brands bare skin. Days of hot, dangerous work. Store in clay-lined iron boxes.

Glacial Diamond.hab: Locked inside ancient glaciers in the far frozen north, pressed for ages under the ice. Blue light glints from deep crevasses where the glacier grinds over bedrock.
Glacial Diamond.how: Climb into crevasses with ropes and ice axes and chip it free over days, braving cold and collapsing ice. Keep it frozen in snow-packed chests or the trapped ice weeps.

Mithral.hab: Silvery veins far down in the oldest mountain roots, often under long-held dwarven halls and vaults. The rock gleams like moonlight and rings when tapped.
Mithral.how: Requires a deep shaft and skilled miners working weeks with steel picks. Ancient claims are often guarded by dwarves, traps or worse. Carry it in sealed sacks.

Starfall Iron.hab: Dark iron cores of large meteorites buried deep beneath old impact craters. The crater floor is fused to glass and compasses spin wildly above the buried mass.
Starfall Iron.how: Sink a shaft through the crater floor over weeks, then saw and smelt the iron apart from slag. It dulls ordinary tools; bring spare picks and a strong forge.

Adamantine.hab: The deepest and hottest mines and the heart of rare great meteorite impacts, in black glossy seams that no ordinary pick can scratch. Heat and bad air grow there.
Adamantine.how: Takes a deep shaft, adamantine-tipped or enchanted tools and months of labour. Cave-ins, heat and rival claimants are constant threats. Store under heavy guard.

Fairy Ring Puffball.hab: Grows in perfect circles on moonlit meadows and woodland clearings, usually after autumn rain. The grass inside the ring is greener and fairy lights flicker at night.
Fairy Ring Puffball.how: Pick by hand at night without stepping inside the ring, and lift gently so it does not burst. Keep in a paper bag; bursting scatters the glittering spores.

Spirit Moss.hab: Soft grey moss on stones and old tree roots along spirit edges, the thin places where the living and spirit worlds touch. Cold spots and whispers mark these places.
Spirit Moss.how: Peel it from the stone with a wooden knife and fingers in a few minutes. It is living and must be kept damp in a closed tin or it dies.

Spirit-Touched Herb.hab: Common herbs growing near shrines, graves and spirit edges that have soaked up faint spirit power. They grow paler than their kin and lean toward cold drafts.
Spirit-Touched Herb.how: Cut with clean shears at dawn and bundle loosely; living herbs wilt if crushed. A quick harvest, best kept in a damp cloth and used within a week.

Comet Dust.hab: Fine shimmering dust that settles on high peaks and open plains after comets pass overhead. It collects in hollows and on snow, glittering faintly at night.
Comet Dust.how: Sweep it up with a soft brush onto parchment the morning after a comet, before wind or rain scatters it. Store in a stoppered glass vial.

Elemental Shard.hab: Small crystal fragments left where elemental spirits burst or passed through, at bonfire sites, lightning strikes, springs and windy cliffs. Each shard buzzes faintly with its element.
Elemental Shard.how: Pick up with tongs or thick gloves, since some burn, freeze or shock. Sort by element and store in separate lined pouches so they do not react.

Ghostcap.hab: Translucent mushrooms in shadowy spirit-edge woods, sprouting on rotting logs and old graves at dusk. You only see them out of the corner of your eye.
Ghostcap.how: Look away and reach sideways to pluck them by feel at dusk; staring makes them vanish. Takes patience. Keep them in a dark pouch until use.

Glass Grass.hab: Transparent, chiming grass covering meadows of the Mirror Realm. It grows thickest where reflected sunlight falls and rings softly when the wind moves through it.
Glass Grass.how: Cut low with a sharp sickle while wearing gloves, as the blades cut skin. Bundle gently; living stalks shatter if bent. Keep in a padded basket.

Gravestone.hab: Dark grey stone taken from ancient graveyards and mass-death sites where hundreds or thousands died. The ground is cold and nothing grows tall among the old markers.
Gravestone.how: Chisel slabs from old headstones and burial cairns over a day, with prayers or offerings to calm the dead. Restless spirits may rise; store wrapped in grave cloth.

Spark Core.hab: Small crackling cores left where lightning strikes hilltops and lone trees in storm country. The ground around them is scorched and hair stands on end nearby.
Spark Core.how: Dig out the scorched earth after a storm using rubber or wooden tools, as bare iron draws a shock. Store in an insulated, wax-lined box.

Animus Stone.hab: Warm, faintly pulsing stones found in the heart of old groves and spirit-haunted hollows, where life energy pools and gathers. Animals stay near them and plants grow lush.
Animus Stone.how: Lift from the soil with bare hands after asking leave of the local spirits; taking one by force makes it go cold. Store in a fur-lined pouch.

Astral Flux.hab: Shimmering motes that drift through astral islands and thin places, blinking in and out of sight. They gather where reality wavers, often near standing stones at night.
Astral Flux.how: Snatch motes with a silk net when they blink back into view, often an hour's patient waiting. Seal at once in a stoppered silver flask or they blink away.

Dreamcap Mushroom.hab: Pale blue mushrooms growing on the drifting astral islands, on soft moss in shaded hollows. Travellers grow drowsy and dream vividly near a patch.
Dreamcap Mushroom.how: Pick them quickly with gloves and a cloth over the nose, as the spores bring sleep. Store in sealed jars away from bedding and anyone resting.

Meridian Glass.hab: Clear glassy crystal that forms along lines of magical power where ley lines cross, often in rock outcrops and old stone circles. Spells cast nearby feel stronger.
Meridian Glass.how: Mine it from shallow outcrops with a crystal pick and steady hands over a day, as cracks let stored magic leak out. Wrap in silk and pack in wool.

Mirror Sand.hab: Fine silvery sand along the shores of the Mirror Realm, where waves of reflected light wash in. Each grain shows a tiny image of the sky.
Mirror Sand.how: Scoop it into sacks with wooden shovels at low tide, an easy morning's work. Keep it dry and covered, as wet sand shows confusing illusions.

Mirrorbloom.hab: A silver-petalled flower that grows on the reflection of still ponds rather than on the bank. Only visible when the water is perfectly calm and clear.
Mirrorbloom.how: Reach into the reflection with a silver ladle at dawn, without breaking the surface; ripples destroy it. Store in a flat dish of still water.

Moonsilver.hab: Pale metal dust that falls during lunar eclipses on open hills and settles in moonstone deposits. It gathers in thin silvery drifts on bare rock.
Moonsilver.how: Sweep it up with silver brushes during and just after the eclipse, before dawn light melts it away. Store in dark glass jars; it can then be forged.

Peachwood.hab: Old peach orchards of spiritual importance, near shrines and temple grounds where offerings were made for generations. The trees bloom out of season and spirits avoid them.
Peachwood.how: Cut fallen or pruned branches with a bronze saw after a prayer of thanks; felling a living tree ruins the warding. Dry slowly in shade for a month.

Rune Stone.hab: Hard grey stone with natural rune-like markings, found in bedrock beneath old stone circles and ancient carved monuments. The marks grow clearer the deeper you dig.
Rune Stone.how: Quarry blocks with picks and wedges over one or two days, cutting along the runes. Breaking a rune spoils its power. Pack in straw for transport.

Starmetal Ingot.hab: Comes from starmetal ore found in small fallen-star craters and shallow seams of star-touched rock. The ore glitters with tiny points like stars at night.
Starmetal Ingot.how: Dig ore from the crater beds with picks over a few days, then smelt it into ingots in a hot forge. Ingots store well wrapped in oiled cloth.

Void-Touched Ore.hab: Grey ore in rock seams where the void has brushed the world, often near sinkholes and places where magic fails. Spells sputter and lights dim above the vein.
Void-Touched Ore.how: Mine with plain iron tools, as enchanted picks lose their magic. A few days of work; keep it in lead-lined crates away from magical items.

Will-o-Wisp Essence.hab: Taken from will-o-wisps that haunt marshes, bogs and misty moors at night, leading travellers astray with their lights. They are drawn to suffering and fear.
Will-o-Wisp Essence.how: Capture a wisp with a cold-iron lantern cage at night, then crystallise its essence over a slow ritual. Risky in deep bogs; store the crystal in dark cloth.

Witchsilver.hab: Tarnish-free silver seams beneath crossroads barrows and fairy mounds, often under old standing stones. Hexes and curses weaken near it and it hums softly.
Witchsilver.how: Dig into the mound with a silver spade, leaving an offering for the fey first. Angry fey may curse thieves. Store in a lined box away from hexed items.

Absence Wire.hab: Thin threads of null metal that run through rock in places where magic simply stops working, often in dead caves and empty vaults. Nothing echoes there.
Absence Wire.how: Pull the threads free from cracked rock with plain pliers over many hours; magic tools fail near it. Coil and store in lead tubes.

Bloodwood.hab: Trees rooted in ancient battlefields and blood-soaked earth, with red grain and dark red sap. The trees grow twisted and crows gather in their branches.
Bloodwood.how: Fell with an axe after appeasing the battlefield dead with rites; the sap stains and stinks of iron. Season the wood for months before working.

Changeling Thyme.hab: Grows around changeling cradles, fey thresholds and doorways where fey have swapped children. Its leaves never look the same twice and smell of your last meal.
Changeling Thyme.how: Pick quietly without naming it aloud, or it changes into a common weed. Bundle with red thread and dry in a dark cupboard; takes only minutes.

Comet Alloy.hab: Formed from comet fragments that struck the ground and fused with local metal, buried beneath streaked, glassy impact scars in hills and plains.
Comet Alloy.how: Dig out the fused chunks with picks over several days, then smelt the alloy free in a very hot forge. Fragments are sharp; use thick gloves.

Echo Stone.hab: Smooth stone lining the walls of Mirror Realm caves, where every sound repeats for minutes. The deeper caves hold the clearest echoes.
Echo Stone.how: Cut it from the cave walls with a chisel in total silence, or the stone stores your noise forever. Wrap in felt and carry without speaking.

Empty Vessel.hab: Hollow stone husks left in places where a soul or power was fully drained, such as abandoned shrines, ruined altars and failed summoning circles.
Empty Vessel.how: Lift with gloves and place in a lined box; never let anything spiritual touch it, as it fills instantly. Easy to collect but hard to find.

Fold Steel.hab: Comes from layered iron ore found in folded rock strata of old mountain ranges, where the stone bends in waves. Each band holds a different grade of iron.
Fold Steel.how: Mine the layered ore with picks over several days, then fold and hammer it many times in a forge. Keep ingots dry and oiled.

Frost Iron.hab: Seams of bitter-cold iron in winter-court glens where snow never melts, deep in fey forests. Frost covers the ground above the ore even in summer.
Frost Iron.how: Mine with fur-lined gloves and wooden-handled picks, as bare skin freezes to it. The winter fey guard these glens; store in straw-packed chests.

Frostwood.hab: Pale trees in frozen northern forests where winter never fully lifts, with white grain and bark coated in hoarfrost. The air near the oldest trunks stings exposed skin.
Frostwood.how: Fell with an axe in deep winter, wearing thick mittens, as the wood stays cold and bites bare hands. Season it outdoors in snow; brought indoors it cracks.

Golem Stone.hab: The core stone at the heart of destroyed golems, found in ruined wizard towers, old guardian halls and battlefields where constructs fell. Faint humming marks a live core.
Golem Stone.how: Break open the fallen golem's chest with hammers and pry the core out whole; some golems still twitch. Takes an hour. Store in an iron-banded crate.

Heartstone.hab: Warm pinkish-red stones at the very centre of ancient forests, where life energy gathers under the oldest trees. Wounds heal faster and flowers bloom out of season nearby.
Heartstone.how: Dig it gently from the roots with a wooden trowel, leaving a gift to the forest; greedy taking angers its spirits. Store in moss-lined boxes.

Moonfire Dust.hab: Made from moonstone found in shallow moonlit streambeds and hill outcrops of the Mysterious realm, then ground into silver dust by an alchemical process under the full moon.
Moonfire Dust.how: Grind moonstone with a silver pestle and alchemist's reagents over a full moon night. Breathing it causes coughing; wear a cloth mask. Store in dark glass vials.

Null Alloy.hab: Comes from dull grey ore in rock seams where magic fades to nothing, often in dead caves and sinkholes. Light spells flicker and fail near the vein.
Null Alloy.how: Mine with plain iron tools over a few days, then smelt with null flux. Magic items carried in should be left outside. Store ingots in lead-lined boxes.

Petrification Resin.hab: Extracted from the eye glands of basilisks, which lair in rocky caves and canyons strewn with stone statues of their victims.
Petrification Resin.how: Kill or subdue a basilisk while blindfolded or using mirrors, then cut out the glands with a fine knife. Stabilise with alchemy within hours; store in sealed jars.

Runesteel.hab: Forged in rune forges from iron dug under rune-carved hills, where the bedrock bears old marks. The best ore comes from seams that already show faint runes.
Runesteel.how: Mine the rune-marked iron with picks, then forge it in a rune forge with a runesmith carving runes during each heat. A week of skilled work.

Silvervein Ore.hab: Bright silver veins running beneath the fey hills, often under old stone rings and hawthorn groves. Fey creatures avoid the ground right above a rich vein.
Silvervein Ore.how: Dig tunnels into the hillside with iron picks over several days. Local fey may harass the miners. Keep the ore in iron-lined chests.

Wisp-Willow.hab: Pale willows in misty fey marshes, with branches that glow softly at night like wisp lights. Travellers easily lose their way among them.
Wisp-Willow.how: Cut thin branches with a silver knife at night, using a rope line to find the way back. The glow fades if the wood is burned or soaked.

Abjuration Ward Stone.hab: Grey crystals at the hearts of ancient defensive enchantments, deep inside fortress ruins with wards still intact. A strange sense of safety grows as you near it.
Abjuration Ward Stone.how: Pass or dispel the active wards first, then lift the stone from its setting with care; this can take days. Breaking the ward wrongly may trigger old traps.

Astral Driftwood.hab: Silvery driftwood carried along astral currents, washing up on the shores of floating islands. Pieces blink in and out of view as they drift.
Astral Driftwood.how: Snag pieces with a hooked pole or net when they blink solid. Can take hours. Tie them down at once or they drift away again.

Cold Iron.hab: Plain iron ore dug from deep, unsunned hillside seams, then worked in specialist forges at low heat. The best ore comes from places fey have never touched.
Cold Iron.how: Mine with ordinary picks, then hammer and smelt at a low temperature over many days. Too much heat ruins its fey-breaking quality. Store in dry sacks.

Collapsed Matter.hab: Tiny, impossibly heavy specks left where gravity magic has gone wrong, in pits and craters where everything nearby bends toward one point.
Collapsed Matter.how: Lift with heavy iron tongs and a reinforced crate; a fist-size lump weighs as much as a horse. Dropping it can break floors or feet.

Conjuration Amber.hab: Golden amber forming at old planar crossing points and summoning circles used for centuries. The boundary there is thin and strange shapes flicker at the edge of sight.
Conjuration Amber.how: Chip it from the circle stones with a silver chisel while a guard watches for creatures slipping through. Work takes hours; store wrapped in warded cloth.

Crystal Spellshard.hab: Clear crystal shards growing in caves along ley lines, inside cracks where magic seeps from the rock. They glow brighter when spells are cast nearby.
Crystal Spellshard.how: Snap shards free with a crystal pick and padded gloves, a few hours' work. Do not cast spells near them while mining. Store packed in wool.

Divination Eye.hab: Opal-like gems with a dark pupil, found in old oracle chambers and places of long prophecy. Visitors there feel watched and see flashes of the future.
Divination Eye.how: Remove carefully with gloves and a blindfold, as looking into it too long brings visions. Takes about an hour; store in a closed velvet pouch.

Dreamsilver.hab: Soft silver seams under the pillows of sleeping hills in fey pockets. Anyone who naps on the hillside dreams vividly and wakes tired.
Dreamsilver.how: Dig quietly with padded picks over a day; waking the hill shakes the tunnel. Do not sleep near the ore. Store in a lined box.

Duskmettle.hab: Found only at places where day and night are always balanced, in perpetual twilight valleys and on boundary ridges. The sky stays the colour of dusk.
Duskmettle.how: Gather the metal from rocks in the twilight with silver tongs; it shifts if carried into full light or dark too quickly. Store in grey cloth.

Elderwood.hab: Elder trees over a thousand years old, standing in remote old forests deep in the realm. Their trunks are huge and the ground hums with nature energy.
Elderwood.how: Only take fallen or freely given branches, with druid blessing; felling an elder brings forest wrath. Season the wood for a year before use.

Enchantment Heartstone.hab: Rose-coloured gems found at sites of ancient compulsion, such as old tyrants' courts and cult halls where minds were bent again and again.
Enchantment Heartstone.how: Handle with gloves for short times only, as long contact makes you agreeable. One person collects while another watches. Store in lead boxes.

Evocation Crystal.hab: Vibrating crystals at ley-line nexuses and old battlefields of great magical wars, where destructive spells were cast for centuries. The ground is scorched and glassy.
Evocation Crystal.how: Pry crystals from the scorched ground with insulated tools over a few hours; they can discharge sparks. Pack in sand-filled boxes.

Fey Silver.hab: Iridescent silver ore found in fey hills and riverbeds, then refined slowly over decades by fey smiths. It always feels slightly damp.
Fey Silver.how: Mine the ore politely, with gifts for the fey, and give it years of fey refining. Theft brings curses. Store wrapped in moss to keep it damp.

Feywild Silver.hab: Silver touched by archfey magic, held in archfey vaults and courts deep in the fey lands. The metal shimmers and shifts colour with nearby moods.
Feywild Silver.how: Must be bargained for or earned from an archfey, never stolen. Deals often cost a promise or a memory. Store away from strong emotions.

Ghostwood.hab: Pale trees in forests on the boundary with the ghostly plane, rooted in both worlds. Their branches fade in and out and cold mist hangs around them.
Ghostwood.how: Cut with a silvered axe when the tree is fully solid, usually at dusk. A careless cut leaves only mist. Season in a dark, cool place.

Illusion Glass.hab: Glass found in fey mirrors and places where reality is thin, often in abandoned halls of mirrors and fey grottos. It reflects things that are not there.
Illusion Glass.how: Find it by touch with closed eyes, since sight cannot tell it from normal glass. Lift with gloves and wrap in black cloth.

Mirror Shard.hab: Sharp fragments in broken Mirror Realm pockets, where small reflected worlds have shattered. Shards lie scattered and show odd reflections of other places.
Mirror Shard.how: Pick up with thick gloves and tongs, as edges cut deep. Do not look into them too long. Store each shard in its own padded sleeve.

Moonmilk Lily.hab: White lilies floating on moonlit fey lakes, opening and dripping white nectar only under moonlight. The water around them glows faintly silver.
Moonmilk Lily.how: Collect nectar at night with a silver spoon into a glass vial; picking the flower stops the flow. Takes a few hours by boat. Keep cool.

Moonpearl.hab: Silver-glowing pearls in giant oysters on the deep ocean floor, ripening only under the new moon. Their faint light shows through dark water.
Moonpearl.how: Dive or use a diving bell on new moon nights, prying oysters open with a pearl knife. Deep water and sea predators are dangerous. Store in silk.

Nature Hearthstone.hab: Green-veined river stones at ancient groves and druid sacred sites tended so long the land itself awoke. Plants lean toward them and streams run clear.
Nature Hearthstone.how: Must be given by the druids or the land spirit after a rite; taking one by force kills the grove. Carry in a moss-lined pouch.

Sorrowstone.hab: Dark blue-grey stones at sites of great tragedy, such as drowned villages, plague towns and massacre fields. A heavy sadness weighs on anyone nearby.
Sorrowstone.how: Gather with gloves after a short rite for the dead; collectors often weep and grow tired. Store in black velvet and work in short shifts.

Soulwood.hab: Trees in forests where many souls departed peacefully, often near old hospices and quiet burial woods. Their grain forms the faces of the dead.
Soulwood.how: Ask the spirits' leave and fell only with a blessed axe; whispers grow loud during the work. Season gently in a quiet room.

Spirit Anchor.hab: Solid cores left at shrines and oath-sites where spirits have been bound by law for generations, often under altar stones or boundary markers.
Spirit Anchor.how: Lift the stone after a priest or shaman releases the bound spirit properly; skipping this frees an angry ghost. Store in a sealed shrine box.

Starlit Quartz.hab: Clear quartz with starry flecks in the rocky cores of astral islands, under thin soil. It glows at night with the light of distant stars.
Starlit Quartz.how: Dig into the island rock with picks and chisels for a day or two. Mine carefully; islands can shift. Wrap in dark cloth to keep its glow.

Starvine.hab: Silver vines that grow on the god-isles floating in the astral sea, climbing over the ruins of dead gods. The tips always point to true north.
Starvine.how: Cut lengths with a silver blade and dry them slowly. God-isles may hold guardians or strange echoes of their gods. Coil and store dry.

Thornmetal.hab: Made in thorn-forests, where thorn tree sap is gathered and used to treat metal. These forests are dense, dark and full of sharp thickets.
Thornmetal.how: Tap thorn tree sap in thick leather armour over many days, then treat metal in it alchemically. Scratches fester easily. Store wrapped in heavy hide.

Witchstone.hab: Dull green stone from places soaked by powerful curse magic, such as hag ruins and cursed villages. Crops fail and animals sicken above the stone.
Witchstone.how: Quarry with picks after a protective ward or charm, as miners can catch stray curses. A few days of grim work. Store in salt-packed crates.

Arcanite.hab: Blue-white solid magic formed where spell residue has collected for centuries, in old wizard towers, academies and battle-magic sites. The air tingles and hair lifts.
Arcanite.how: Scrape or chip it from walls and floors with insulated tools over days; it can discharge raw magic. Store in lead-lined cases.

Astral Silver.hab: Silver found adrift in the astral sea and on the rocky shores of astral islands, glowing with the energy of thought. It moves toward strong minds.
Astral Silver.how: Reach it by astral travel or ship, then pull it in with nets and grapples. Psychic storms are a danger. Store in cloth-lined boxes.

Darksteel.hab: Black iron ore mined in total darkness in the shadow plane, where no light has ever shone. The rock is cold and shadows move on their own.
Darksteel.how: Mine and forge it in complete darkness; any light ruins the steel. Miners work blind by touch for weeks. Store in light-proof crates.

Dreadwood.hab: Twisted trees at the edge of reality where alien realms press close. The grain forms faces and eyes, and travellers suffer bad dreams nearby.
Dreadwood.how: Fell quickly with an axe while avoiding long looks at the grain; madness and fear are real dangers. Store wrapped in heavy canvas.

Dreamstone.hab: Soft lavender stones in regions where sleep magic has gathered for decades, such as enchanted forests and old sleeping-curse castles. Visitors yawn and drift off.
Dreamstone.how: Collect with a partner who keeps you awake; falling asleep can trap you in dreams. Store in a lidded box away from beds.

Faerie Gold.hab: Gleaming gold heaped in fey hoards hidden in hollow hills and under bridges. By daylight much of it turns to leaves and nuts.
Faerie Gold.how: Win or bargain it from the fey; stolen gold brings curses. Bind it with a binding agent before dawn or it becomes leaves.

Frost Elemental Ice.hab: Never-melting ice left by water elementals in frozen caves and icy lakes. It stays bitterly cold and spreads frost across the ground nearby.
Frost Elemental Ice.how: Chip off pieces with an iron chisel, wearing thick gloves and furs. Elementals may guard their ice. Store in insulated iron boxes.

Hexite.hab: A grey metal worked only in hag workshops, hidden in swamps and dark woods. The smelting uses curses, so the area is full of bad luck.
Hexite.how: Buy, steal or trade it from a hag, which is always dangerous. Theft brings curses. Store with protective charms and handle with gloves.

Hollowhill Root.hab: Pale roots growing inside hollow hills, through the walls between mirrors and the fey pockets behind them. They glow faintly in the dark tunnels.
Hollowhill Root.how: Enter the hollow hill and cut roots with a silver knife, keeping an eye on the way out. Time can pass oddly. Store in damp earth.

Livewood.hab: Rare trees that keep living after harvest, growing in hidden glades where the soil is rich and the air full of life. Saplings sprout from every fallen twig.
Livewood.how: Cut with care and keep the wood in soil and water, as it is still alive. Bond with it slowly over weeks. Store in a pot.

Manacite.hab: Crystals in caves and rock beneath wild magic zones, where magic constantly surges. Strange lights and random spells appear above ground.
Manacite.how: Mine during calm hours with crystal picks over a day or two. Wild surges can strike miners. Store in warded boxes.

Mirrorsteel.hab: Steel found on the far side of old mirrors and still ponds, in strange reflected rooms behind the glass. It reflects things not in the room.
Mirrorsteel.how: Step through the mirror with a guide and pull the steel back out before the reflection closes. Getting trapped is the danger. Wrap in black cloth.

Necromancy Stone.hab: Black, slowly pulsing stones deep under ancient burial grounds and mass-death sites, where necrotic energy had nowhere to go. Undead rise often there.
Necromancy Stone.how: Dig into the burial ground with picks under guard, as undead attack diggers. A few days of work. Store in blessed, salt-lined boxes.

Prismaite.hab: Colour-cycling crystals in caves and rock beneath wild magic zones, where colours flicker across the stone. Each change brings a different element.
Prismaite.how: Mine during calm moments with gloves and crystal picks. Its colour shifts can burn, freeze or shock you. Store each piece in a separate warded pouch.

Psionic Mindgem.hab: Flawless spheres left on old psionic battlefields and in the ruined cities of brain-eating psionic horrors. Headaches, whispers and stray thoughts fill the air there.
Psionic Mindgem.how: Search the ruins with a mind shield or iron circlet, lifting gems with gloves. Lingering psychic echoes can stun or madden. Store each in a lead-lined pouch.
