Inanestone.how: Pry free with a padded bar rather than striking, since blows turn it to dust; brush crumbling edges into sealed vials and wrap the core in oiled leather. A day or more.

Nanostone.hab: Threaded through deep cracks in Outer Realm bedrock where the Nano Rune pools, a dark shimmering dust that seeps slowly along fissures and gathers in still pockets.
Nanostone.how: Draw it out of cracks with a fine-mesh scoop and a tightly woven sack, working slowly so it clumps; store in stoppered glass, since it flows out through any seam.

Negationstone.hab: Deep Outer Realm veins where the Negation Rune pools, inside dead-silent galleries where torches dim and spells sputter; a sudden hush and failing light warn that it is near.
Negationstone.how: Mine by hand with mundane steel tools and lamps of plain oil, since magic lights and spells fail beside it; haul it out in lead-lined crates over several days.

Nightmarestone.hab: Seams of swirling purple stone in Outer Realm deeps where the Nightmare Rune pools; miners report terrible dreams for nights before they ever strike the vein.
Nightmarestone.how: Work in short waking shifts, never sleeping within a mile of the seam; chip it free with a pick and wrap it in black wool soaked in salt water to dull its visions.

Obsessionstone.hab: Narrow dark red veins in Outer Realm rock where the Obsession Rune pools, every glint inside pointing toward one fixed spot; workers near it grow fixated on single tasks.
Obsessionstone.how: Cut around the seam rather than into it, lifting it out whole on a sledge over two days; take turns at the work so no miner stares into it too long.

Overdrive Stone.hab: Hot, cracked red veins deep in the Outer Realm where the Overdrive Rune pools, throbbing faster as diggers approach; scorched rock and racing hearts mark the spot.
Overdrive Stone.how: Break it out quickly with a heavy pick in under an hour, then drop it into cold water and a ceramic jar; held too long, it burns itself and its holder out.

Pickstone.hab: Wedge-shaped crystals set point-down in hard Outer Realm bedrock where the Pickaxe Rune pools, often under quarries where broken stone lies in neat heaps no one stacked.
Pickstone.how: Use a pickstone already won to split the rock around the next, as ordinary picks blunt first; lift each wedge free in a day and sheathe its point in thick leather.

Plasmastone.hab: Crackling violet-white veins in deep Outer Realm galleries where the Plasma Rune pools; the air there smells of lightning and the tunnel walls are glazed smooth by heat.
Plasmastone.how: Mine in insulated gear with ceramic-headed tools, never bare metal, which arcs and melts; set each piece in a clay crucible packed with sand and carry it out quickly.

Pridestone.hab: Upright violet crystals rooted in the floors of Outer Realm palace ruins and the vaults beneath, where the Pride Rune pools; they glow brighter whenever someone nearby boasts.
Pridestone.how: Work in total silence, since any boast flares it hot; cut the crystal free at its base with a fine saw over a day and pack it upright in a padded case.

Rebel Stone.hab: Cracked black seams under the rubble of fallen Outer Realm thrones, where the Rebellion Rune pools; red sparks flare in the rock whenever an order is shouted nearby.
Rebel Stone.how: Dig with no foreman giving commands, since orders make it spit sparks and shatter; each miner works by choice and agreement, taking two days to clear the rubble and vein.

Screwstone.hab: Jammed inside giant broken engines in Outer Realm machine ruins and in the bedrock beneath them, where the Screw Rune pools; spiral grooves score the surrounding metal.
Screwstone.how: Turn it out of its seat counterclockwise with a long iron wrench rather than prying, a slow half day per stone; store it lying on its side so it cannot bore downward.

Shieldstone.hab: Round grey nodules in Outer Realm forge mountains, set among veins of iron and steel where the Shield Rune pools; the rock around them deflects picks oddly.
Shieldstone.how: Dig around each nodule instead of striking it, since blows glance off; lever it out with crowbars over a day or two and roll it, rim down, onto a reinforced cart.

Skipstone.hab: Flat grey stones skipping endlessly across still Outer Realm lakes of silver mist, gathered where the Skip Rune pools; they hover a finger's width above whatever they cross.
Skipstone.how: Wait in a flat boat and catch one mid-skip with a weighted net, then press it into a lidded box at once; a missed catch can take a whole day to come round again.

Skullstone.hab: Buried in the soil and rock beneath old Outer Realm battlegrounds and summoners' trophy halls, in pockets where the Skull Rune pools; bones lie thick in the earth above.
Skullstone.how: Excavate slowly with trowels and brushes like a grave dig, two or three days per find; speak respectfully to the dead there and wrap each skull in grave linen.

Slowstone.hab: Sunk deep in Outer Realm tar pits and ancient resin swamps where the Slowness Rune pools; the tar around it moves even slower than normal and holds trapped creatures intact.
Slowstone.how: Fish it up on a long hooked pole from a firm raft, a slow job of a day or more; tie yourself to the raft, since the tar slows anyone who slips in.

Starstone.hab: Under the floors of scorched Outer Realm craters where stars fell and burned out, in white-gold veins where the Star Rune pools; the crater ground stays warm all night.
Starstone.how: Shaft down through the glassy crater bed with heat-proof picks, two or three days of work; handle with thick hide gloves and store in iron boxes packed with ash.

Stress Stone.hab: Ash-coloured seams in the crushing depths of the Outer Realm where the Stress Rune pools, under enormous rock pressure; the tunnel walls groan and spall as one approaches.
Stress Stone.how: Shore the shaft heavily, then ease it out with gentle wedges and no hammering, since sudden pressure fractures it; ride it up in a padded cradle and never stack anything on it.

Unravelstone.hab: Tangled fibrous seams in the far Outer Realm where the Unravel Rune pools, often in loosening cliffs whose strata fray apart like old rope.
Unravelstone.how: Wind the loose threads onto a wooden spool as you cut, and never let anyone tug at one; bind each piece tightly with waxed cord and store it in a sealed tin.

Verbalstone.hab: Smooth grey veins in the walls of Outer Realm speaking halls and oracle caves where the Verbal Rune pools; spoken words return as faint echoes from the rock.
Verbalstone.how: Speak to the seam softly and cut where the echo is clearest, using a quiet chisel over a day; keep it wrapped in felt so it does not repeat every conversation.

Wendigostone.hab: Pale, pitted veins under the starving frozen wastes of the Outer Realm where the Wendigo Rune pools; frost thickens around the site and travellers there feel gnawing hunger.
Wendigostone.how: Dig in short shifts by a large fire, eating well before each one, and handle it only with fur-lined tongs; it draws warmth and hunger from bare hands. Store in fleece.

Zerostone.hab: Hollow black rings lodged in empty pockets of the Outer Realm bedrock where the Zero Rune pools; the hole at each ring's centre shows nothing at all.
Zerostone.how: Cut out the rock around the ring, never reaching through its centre, which numbs a hand for days; lift it with a wooden rod threaded through and store on a peg.

Orbit Orichalcum.hab: Chunks of orichalcum circling in rings around dead worlds in the Outer Realm, drifting in slow orbit around anything heavy; they cluster near the densest debris.
Orbit Orichalcum.how: Fly or sail the ring and snag pieces with weighted chain nets, then anchor them to a heavy iron block so they orbit it instead of you. Days of patient hunting.

Unknown Amber.hab: Lumps of amber at The Edge of the Outer Realm, where reality frays; things trapped inside should not exist, and the ground near it shifts in ways eyes refuse to follow.
Unknown Amber.how: Approach roped to a fixed anchor and gather by feel with gloved hands, eyes partly shut; seal it in lead boxes at once and never study its contents closely. Many days' travel.

Eclipse Bloom.hab: On the dark faces of shadowed Outer Realm moons, rising only during an eclipse; a black flower ringed with fire, growing from cold dust where light never falls.
Eclipse Bloom.how: Wait for an eclipse, often months, then cut the stem with an obsidian blade in the minutes of darkness; carry it in a closed, light-proof clay jar before light returns.

Edge Iron.hab: Deep in the bedrock at The Edge of the Outer Realm, where the realm's laws thin to a fringe; veins run through rock that seems to reach endlessly outward.
Edge Iron.how: Sink a shaft at The Edge over weeks with master-forged tools, guarded against what drifts in from beyond; carry ingots back in rune-sealed crates on a long, hard road.

Stillstone.hab: Found everywhere in the Void, from loose slabs to the bedrock below; each piece stays exactly where it last came to rest and resists every push.
Stillstone.how: Quarry it in place with chisels and wedges, a few hours per block; it will not move once cut, so set it on a sledge before the last stroke frees it.

Hush Iron.hab: Silent drifts and shallow seams at the Void's edge, in dull grey lodes where even falling rock makes no sound; look for strangely quiet ground.
Hush Iron.how: Mine with an ordinary pick in a day; it rings silent, so post a lookout who watches rather than listens for collapses. Store wrapped in cloth like any iron.

Pale Lichen.hab: Colourless crusts on floating Void debris, growing on nothing at all in the gaps between drifting rocks; it shows as faint pale shapes against empty dark.
Pale Lichen.how: Reach it from a tethered skiff or line and scrape it into a jar with a bone spatula; a half day's work, keeping a hand on the tether at all times.

Void Ice.hab: Cold pockets in the Void where heat has fled entirely, forming clear blocks of absolute-cold ice; frost appears on anything brought near and breath freezes mid-air.
Void Ice.how: Chip it free with long-handled tools in layered furs and thick mittens, never bare skin; carry it in double-walled, wool-packed boxes and work in short shifts.

Nullthorn.hab: Dense Void thickets of grey thorny shrub growing in drifting soil; the air in them feels drained, and spellcasters there grow faint and clumsy.
Nullthorn.how: Cut stems with plain iron shears in heavy leather gloves over a few hours; a prick bleeds magic from the blood, so casters should not harvest. Bundle in hide.

Pale Lead.hab: Grey shoals of the Void where colourless lead lodes lie beneath drifting sediment; scrying and sight fail over them, so maps of the area are always blank.
Pale Lead.how: Dig through the shoal sediment to the lode with shovels and picks over a day or two; cast it into ingots on site and keep it away from your own wards.

Spin Crystal.hab: Spinning crystals caught in slow Void spin currents, whirling in place where the currents eddy; light around them bends in spirals.
Spin Crystal.how: Enter the current with a tether and close a padded cage around one, letting it spin itself still over an hour; a hard grab breaks wrists. Store it in its cage.

Nullsteel.hab: Locked inside drifting debris of the Void, in dark seams through tumbling rock chunks; the debris bearing it moves against the general drift.
Nullsteel.how: Moor to a drifting chunk and tunnel into it with mundane tools over several days, anchoring carefully; magic fails nearby, so all gear must work without it.

Absence Fern.hab: Hollows of the Void, shallow dips where even the dark feels thinner; fern fronds grow with holes where leaves should be, often hidden by their own gaps.
Absence Fern.how: Find it by touch, sweeping slowly with gloved hands, then cut it at the base with a silver knife; press the fronds flat between slates. A full day per find.

Dead Star Iron.hab: In the dense remains of dead stars in the Void, buried in crushed iron cores where gravity drags hard; ships and climbers feel heavier the closer they come.
Dead Star Iron.how: Approach in gravity-braced harnesses and mine with heavy-headed picks over many days; pieces weigh many times their size, so haul them in reinforced cradles with winches.

Silence Steel.hab: Deep hollows of the Void where light goes out, in steel veins lining their walls; spells cast nearby fade into a faint chill instead of taking effect.
Silence Steel.how: Descend into the dark by rope and feel along the walls for the cold; cut it out with mundane steel saws over days, carrying oil lamps, as magic light dies.

Starless Lotus.hab: Black lotuses floating on dead-star pools in the Void, where stars died and left still, dark water; the sky above them shows nothing at all.
Starless Lotus.how: Wade or punt into the pool and cut the stem below water with a long hooked blade; dry it in darkness, as light withers it. Pools often hide gravity drops.

Timeworn Sand.hab: Eddies in the Void where time loops and slows, piling fine sand that has aged for ages in moments; dunes there shift in strange, uneven rhythms.
Timeworn Sand.how: Scoop it quickly with a sealed brass ladle into hourglass flasks, staying only minutes, since lingering ages the body; time spent there may differ from outside.

Balance Silver.hab: Balance points of the Void, where pulls from every direction cancel out; silver veins grow in perfect symmetry through rock that hangs perfectly still.
Balance Silver.how: Cut matching amounts from both sides of the vein at once over several days, keeping it level; uneven cuts topple the whole mass. Store each bar on a balanced rack.

Calibration Stone.hab: Precisely cut seams in Void bedrock where the Calibration Rune pools, every fracture meeting at an exact angle; the tunnels there run perfectly straight and square.
Calibration Stone.how: Measure with a square and plumb before every cut and split it only along its facet lines, two or three days of exacting work; pack in fitted, felt-lined cases.

Corruption Stone.hab: Void cracks where Hell's touch seeps in and the Corruption Rune pools, with black veins spreading through the rock; the stone around rots and smells of sulphur.
Corruption Stone.how: Mine in sealed gloves and masks, burning or salting any exposed skin contact at once; store in salt-packed iron chests, and swap tools often, as they blacken and rot.

Darksight Stone.hab: Smoky seams in the endless dark of the Void where the Dark Vision Rune pools; in total dark a faint pupil-shaped glint seems to watch from the rock.
Darksight Stone.how: Work by touch in complete darkness, since light hides it, cutting slowly with a fine chisel over two days; wrap it in black velvet and store it in a closed box.

Dullahanstone.hab: Beneath the endless black roads of the Void where the Dullahan Rune pools, in veins below roadbeds; a faint glow hovers just above the surface where they lie.
Dullahanstone.how: Dig under the road only when no headless riders are passing, a watch of days; cut it out quickly and cover the hovering glow with a hood before travelling.

Elasticstone.hab: Stretchy blue-grey seams deep in the Void where the Elastic Rune pools, bulging and flexing in the rock walls as pressure shifts around them.
Elasticstone.how: Saw it with a fine-toothed blade, since picks bounce back hard; tie the cut ends to stakes so they do not snap back, and store it coiled in a crate.

Endingstone.hab: Black seams in the silent stretches of the Void where the Ending Rune pools; lamps, songs and efforts all seem to wind down near it.
Endingstone.how: Work fast in short shifts, finishing each task before it fades, and use a fresh team for the final lift; store in a sealed box and keep it apart from candles.

Eternalstone.hab: Flawless silver seams in the oldest and quietest layers of the Void where the Eternal Rune pools, unchanged since the realm began and buried very deep.
Eternalstone.how: No tool scratches it, so cut away the rock around it over a week and lift it whole; wrap it in plain linen, as nothing will harm it.

Famestone.hab: Glowing stones scattered on the vast fields of the Void where the Fame Rune pools; every eye is drawn to them, and gathered crowds of drifting things watch over them.
Famestone.how: Approach under cover and drop a dark hood over the glow before lifting it, as every watcher turns to look; carry it hidden in a thick cloth bag.

Icestone.hab: Clear blue veins in the Void where Undine's remains froze and the Ice Rune pools; the rock holds faint shapes of old water and the air frosts as you descend.
Icestone.how: Chip it out with heavy-gloved hands and bronze picks, since iron freezes to it; work in short warm shifts and store it in straw-packed, wool-lined boxes.

Idealstone.hab: Crystal-clear seams in quiet Void expanses where the Ideals Rune pools; looking into the rock shows each viewer an image of the virtue or sin they hold dearest.
Idealstone.how: Mine with eyes downcast and cut by touch, since staring traps the viewer for hours; wrap it in opaque cloth at once and carry it in a closed case.

Immunitystone.hab: Seamless grey-white nodules deep in Void bedrock where the Immunity Rune pools, untouched by anything around them; rust, rot and heat never mark the rock beside it.
Immunitystone.how: Nothing scratches or burns it, so carve away the surrounding stone over several days and lift the nodule whole; store in any box, since it takes no harm.

Legendstone.hab: Shimmering silver veins in Void bedrock where the Legend Rune pools; the rock face shows scenes of heroic deeds that grow grander each time someone looks away.
Legendstone.how: Carve it out over two days while telling true tales of your own deeds, which the stone favours; wrap it in a cloak and do not boast while carrying it.

Realstone.hab: Plain seams in the Void where all other laws thin out and the Reality Rune pools; everything around them looks sharper and more solid, though the stone itself goes unnoticed.
Realstone.how: Search for the sharpest-looking rock and dig there with steady attention, since eyes slide off it; mark each piece with chalk at once and store it in a labelled box.

Releasestone.hab: Loose stones drifting in the Void where bindings have broken and the Release Rune pools; snapped chains and burst cages float nearby, and nothing tied stays tied there.
Releasestone.how: Catch it by hand rather than by net or rope, which it slips; carry it only in a holder shaped by a master craftsman, or it escapes within the hour.

Telepathy Stone.hab: Lavender seams in the silent, thought-filled drift of the Void where the Telepathy Rune pools; miners near them hear stray whispers of each other's thoughts.
Telepathy Stone.how: Mine in calm, focused shifts and keep minds quiet to avoid confusion; wrap it in thick wool away from your head, and store each piece apart from the others.

Turnstone.hab: Round stones spinning in place within the drifting fields of the Void where the Turn Rune pools; each turns slowly on its own and stirs a faint spiral of dust.
Turnstone.how: Slip a cupped wooden bowl beneath it and let it turn freely as you lift; never grip it, or it wrenches the wrist. Carry it in a bowl-lined box.

Unlit Gold.hab: Lodes in deep Void caverns where no light ever reaches; the gold reflects nothing and appears as gold-shaped holes in the cave wall.
Unlit Gold.how: Find it by touch and by the cold gaps in lamplight, then cut it out with fine picks over many days; wrap each nugget in white cloth so it can be seen.

Worldstone.hab: Heavy layered seams in the deep foundations of the Void where the World Rune pools; tiny mountains, seas and forests show inside, and the rock above feels like solid ground.
Worldstone.how: Cut it free in whole layers with broad saws over several days, keeping each slab level so its tiny seas do not spill; carry it on padded stretchers.

Wraithstone.hab: Smoke-grey seams in empty Void chambers where spirits linger and the Wraith Rune pools; cold drafts move with no wind and lights gutter as the restless dead pass.
Wraithstone.how: Mine with silvered tools while a guard keeps the wraiths at bay; it is partly intangible, so cup it in silver-lined gloves and store it in a silver box.

Gravity Knot.hab: At the bottom of gravity wells in the Void, where pull grows crushing; the knot is a tight core of bent force that drags light and dust toward it.
Gravity Knot.how: Descend on reinforced cables with weighted harnesses over days, then bind the knot in a cage of rune-forged iron; ascent is slow, and cut lines mean a fatal fall.

Oblivion Poppy.hab: Grey poppies growing in sparse clusters in the deep Void, far from any light; travellers who linger in their scent forget why they came.
Oblivion Poppy.how: Harvest with a cloth mask soaked in sharp herbs and a written list of your task; snip the pods into sealed jars and leave quickly, a few hours' work.

Absence Adamant.hab: At the edges of true nothing in the Void, where raw adamant is mostly not there; it shows as a faint outline that erases the space it touches.
Absence Adamant.how: Cut only with tools of other adamant, over weeks, without touching it, since it erases flesh; store it in a nest of nothingness-warded cloth and expect loss of life.

Orbit Stone.hab: Stones circling the largest Void gravity wells in tight, fast orbits, where the pull is strongest; they whip past like sling stones in endless loops.
Orbit Stone.how: Match their orbit with a braced, armoured craft over many attempts, then catch one in a heavy net; a mistimed grab can shatter limbs or drag one into the well.

Zero Root.hab: Down on the Void's floor, rooted into the space between spaces; pale roots vanish into gaps in nothing, found only after the long and lightless descent.
Zero Root.how: Follow a root back with a silver thread tied to your waist and cut it with an adamant knife over a day; store in a box warded against slipping away.

Inward Bloom.hab: Shallow spiral caves of the Inner Void, growing in the turns where the walls curl inward; its petals stay tightly closed and lean toward the spiral's centre.
Inward Bloom.how: Pluck it by hand in a few minutes and keep it closed; forcing the petals open ruins it. Carry it in a small wooden box.

Absence Stone.hab: Common everywhere in the Inner Void, from loose rubble to bedrock, though hard to perceive; eyes slide past it and maps often leave it out.
Absence Stone.how: Quarry it by touch with ordinary picks in a few hours, marking blocks with chalk as soon as they are cut, or they are lost again in the rubble.

Coreseed.hab: Kernel caverns of the Inner Void, where dense black seeds gather on cave floors in low hollows; they sink into soft ground under their own weight.
Coreseed.how: Dig them out of the floor with a trowel and lift them with both hands, since they weigh far more than they look; carry in a stout leather pouch.

Inward Iron.hab: Spiral caverns of the Inner Void, in iron lodes that coil around the cavern's centre; the ore bends inward the longer it sits.
Inward Iron.how: Mine with ordinary picks over a day, then bind the ore straight with bands while someone holds it in focused thought; left alone it curls in a week.

Zero Iron.hab: Seams along the border between the Void and Inner Void, where weightless iron floats free inside cracked rock; the ore drifts upward when split loose.
Zero Iron.how: Mine with a net over the cut, since freed pieces float away; tie each piece down in weighted sacks and haul it out in a day or two.

Empty Crystal.hab: Deep Inner Void caves where absence gathers into clear crystals; they seem hollow, and the space around them feels drained of meaning.
Empty Crystal.how: Cut it out with mundane tools over two days, as magic fails near it; store in a sealed box and never place spell components inside with it.

Recursion Fern.hab: Looping tunnels of the Inner Void, where ferns whose fronds are made of smaller fronds forever grow along walls that repeat themselves.
Recursion Fern.how: Cut a single frond near its base with fine scissors, not the whole plant, which tangles endlessly; mark the way out, as the tunnels loop back. Half a day.

Collapse Thistle.hab: Inner Void collapse zones, where ground and air keep falling inward; thistles grow among the debris, standing still while everything around them shrinks.
Collapse Thistle.how: Cover the head with a jar first and seal it before cutting the stem, since it implodes to dust when picked; leave quickly before the ground folds in.

Underlight Silver.hab: Pockets beneath the Inner Void crust, where silver glows from within yet lights nothing around it; the glow can be seen only by looking straight at it.
Underlight Silver.how: Tunnel under the crust over several days, following the glow with your own lamp; carry each nugget in a closed tin, as it guides nothing.

Zero-glass.hab: Near the source of Zero in the Inner Void, where glassy shards form in the deepest null fields; magic dies in the air and the ground turns smooth and glassy.
Zero-glass.how: Gather the shards with gloved hands and mundane tongs over a day, as spells fail around it; wrap each in felt and store apart from any enchanted items.

Nullpearl.hab: Silent Inner Void pools where no ripple ever stirs; pearls rest in soft beds on the pool floor, and any spell cast over the water simply dies.
Nullpearl.how: Dive or reach in with a long ladle, as magic breathing fails here; take one pearl at a time and store each in a lead-lined pouch.

Ouroboros Steel.hab: Ring-shaped lodes in Inner Void tunnels that end where they begin; the ore forms closed circles in the rock and regrows anything cut from it within a day.
Ouroboros Steel.how: Cut a segment from the ring and leave before the ore heals over in a day; store pieces apart, as they try to rejoin into a loop.

Ouroboros Vine.hab: Along the walls of Inner Void ouroboros tunnels, growing in perfect loops that eat their own tips; travellers find the same vine at every turn.
Ouroboros Vine.how: Cut a loop cleanly in two places with a sharp knife and tie the ends apart, or they rejoin; mark the way back, since the tunnels circle.

Assembly Stone.hab: Deposits of interlocking gear-like facets in Inner Void seams where the Assembly Rune pools; split rock clicks softly and slowly reforms behind the miners.
Assembly Stone.how: Cut and lift quickly in one shift before it reassembles, using a team; store pieces in separate boxes so they do not click back together.

Battle Axe Stone.hab: Inner Void cliffs that fall away in clean, axe-cut faces, where the Battle Axe Rune pools in crescent-shaped seams; the rock edges are razor sharp.
Battle Axe Stone.how: Rope down the cliff in thick leather armour and cut along the crescent with heavy wedges over two days; lower it in a padded sling, edge outward.

Blightstone.hab: Under dead Inner Void wastelands where nothing has grown in ages and the Blight Rune pools; the ground above is dry, grey and cracked.
Blightstone.how: Mine in sealed boots and gloves, keeping all herbs and food far away, since it withers living things; store it in a stone box lined with salt.

Boystone.hab: Small bright stones in Inner Void hollows where youth collects and the Boy Rune pools; plants and faces near the hollow look fresher and younger.
Boystone.how: Pick them from the hollow walls with a small chisel in a few hours; do not linger too long, or you start to grow younger. Store in a tin.

Clarity Stone.hab: Flawless clear seams in Inner Void caverns where the Clarity Rune pools, letting light pass through every surface; the cave walls look like glass.
Clarity Stone.how: Cut with a diamond saw and a fine file over days, keeping it free of scratches; wrap in soft white silk to avoid clouding its faces.

Daggerstone.hab: Thin needle-sharp shards along blade-like ridges in the Inner Void where the Dagger Rune pools; the rock hums faintly when wind passes the ridges.
Daggerstone.how: Snap shards from the ridge with padded tongs in heavy gauntlets, an hour or two of careful work; sheathe each one in a leather case.

Entropystone.hab: Grey seams in decaying reaches of the Inner Void where the Entropy Rune pools; the stone crumbles to dust and then reforms in slow cycles.
Entropystone.how: Time the cut for the moment it reforms, gathering it quickly into a tight jar; tools rust and fail fast there, so bring spares.

Failurestone.hab: Cracked black seams in the broken lands of the Inner Void where the Failure Rune pools; tools slip and steps falter as one draws near.
Failurestone.how: Work slowly with tethered tools and two hands on every grip; it slips free, so catch it in a net below the cut. Store in a locked box.

Falsestone.hab: Shifting seams in twisting Inner Void tunnels where the False Rune pools; the stone looks different to each viewer and the tunnels deceive the eye.
Falsestone.how: Mark it with chalk and trust touch over sight; one miner cuts while another checks the shape by hand. Store in a labelled box.

Guaranteestone.hab: Flawless clear seams in the deepest calm pockets of the Inner Void where the Guarantee Rune pools; the rock there is still and certain.
Guaranteestone.how: Plan every cut before you begin, then lift it whole in one careful week; once removed it stays exactly as it is. Store in a padded case.

Hopestone.hab: Pale gold seams deep in the Inner Void where the Hope Rune pools; a single bright point glows in the rock even in total darkness.
Hopestone.how: Follow the light by descent through deep dark tunnels over days, then cut with a gentle chisel; keep it in a lantern case, as it lights the way out.

Jiangshistone.hab: Stiff grey seams beneath frozen Inner Void graveyards where the Jiangshi Rune pools; red talisman-like markings show in the rock and the dead hop nearby.
Jiangshistone.how: Dig with paper wards pasted on your tools and hold your breath when the hoppers pass; store it wrapped in red cloth with a written charm.

Lengthstone.hab: Rod-like seams in the Inner Void where the Longer Rune pools, running in one unbroken grain far through the rock; it grows longer each time it is measured.
Lengthstone.how: Do not measure it; cut quickly at both ends with a saw over a day and carry it in a long open crate, which it may outgrow.

Lineagestone.hab: Deep Inner Void seams among the remains of forgotten first ancestors, where the Race Rune pools; each viewer sees their own bloodline in its grain.
Lineagestone.how: Cut it with respect at ancestral sites, leaving offerings for the dead; work over two days and wrap it in clean linen.

Lockstone.hab: Dense slate-grey seams in the Inner Void where the Lock Rune pools, shaped like interlocking tumblers; adjoining pieces clamp shut and hold fast.
Lockstone.how: Keep cut pieces apart with wooden spacers, since two touching cannot be pried apart without the holder's will; carry each in its own pouch.

Magnetstone.hab: Heavy iron-black seams in the Inner Void where the Magnetic Rune pools; iron filings stand up in lines along the rock and tools pull toward it.
Magnetstone.how: Mine with bronze, stone or wooden tools, since iron sticks to it; store it in a wooden box far from steel weapons and armour.

Moodstone.hab: Grey seams in the Inner Void where the Mental State Rune pools, shifting colour with the moods of those nearby; workers there feel their feelings strengthened.
Moodstone.how: Mine in calm teams who rest often, since strong feelings make it flare; wrap it in grey cloth and keep it from anxious hands.

Mudstone.hab: Damp brown seams in the Inner Void where the Mud Rune pools; the stone never fully dries and squishes slightly before firming again.
Mudstone.how: Dig it out with broad shovels over a day, pressing it firm before lifting; store in clay jars kept damp, or it cracks.

Precisionstone.hab: Perfectly cut crystal seams in the Inner Void where the Precision Rune pools; its edges slice light into neat beams across the tunnel walls.
Precisionstone.how: Cut exactly along its own edges with fine chisels over days, as any wrong cut ruins it; store in a fitted wooden case.

Pulsestone.hab: Deep crimson seams in the Inner Void where the Pulse Rune pools; a slow audible throb shakes dust loose from the walls in time with its beat.
Pulsestone.how: Cut between beats with a sharp chisel over a day, timing each stroke; carry it in a padded box that muffles its throb.

Saberstone.hab: Curved steel-blue seams in the Inner Void where old sword strikes left cuts in empty space and the Saber Rune pools; the rock bears clean crescent slashes.
Saberstone.how: Cut along the slash in heavy gauntlets over two days, as the edge is keen; sheathe it in a curved leather scabbard.

Servitude Stone.hab: Beneath abandoned workhouses of the first empires in the Inner Void, where the Servitude Rune pools; grey stones lie collared by dark bands.
Servitude Stone.how: Dig in short shifts and never accept orders while near it, as it breeds obedience; store it in a heavy iron box with a lock.

Staticstone.hab: Grainy grey seams beneath silent Inner Void fields where the Static Rune pools; the rock crackles and hisses, and hair stands on end above it.
Staticstone.how: Mine with wooden-handled tools in rubber-soled boots, grounding yourself often; store it in a glass jar lined with wool.

Steadystone.hab: Balanced grey stones in the Inner Void where the Stabilise Rune pools, set like keystones that hold broken laws together; removing one shakes everything around it.
Steadystone.how: Shore up the area first with braces and wards, then lift it out over days; it never tips, so carry it level in a padded crate.

Undead Summoning Stone.hab: Bone-white seams green-veined beneath the deepest crypt fields of the Inner Void, where the Undead Summoning Rune pools; the soil smells of the grave and the dead stir.
Undead Summoning Stone.how: Dig under guard with holy water and silvered tools over several days; wrap it in blessed linen and store in a sealed stone coffer.

Worshipstone.hab: Golden seams under ancient Inner Void temples where the Worship Rune pools; faint prayer marks cover it and it glows brighter during devotion.
Worshipstone.how: Pray at the temple before cutting, then work slowly with a silver chisel over two days; store it in a carved shrine box.

Kernel Gold.hab: Deep in the Inner Void kernel, the innermost core of the realm; dense gold lodes lie where meaning gathers, changing the weight of words spoken nearby.
Kernel Gold.how: Reach the kernel after a dangerous journey of weeks and mine it in silence, since spoken words grow crushingly heavy; carry ingots in rune-locked chests.

Kernel Lotus.hab: Floating on the kernel pool at the core of the Inner Void, a dark lotus that drinks in light; the pool is pitch black and very cold.
Kernel Lotus.how: Approach without lamps, since it drains them, and cut the stem with a silver blade; store it in a light-proof jar and leave the pool quickly.

Unmade Silver.hab: Near the source of Emptiness in the Inner Void, in silver seams that keep shifting between being and unbeing; the rock there flickers and changes.
Unmade Silver.how: Mine in teams with chaos wards over many days, cutting when the seam is solid; store in a rune-sealed chest checked daily.

Final Shard.hab: At the source of Zero, the last point in the Inner Void before nothing; a single shard of something long gone, guarded by emptiness that unmakes intruders.
Final Shard.how: Reach it after a long, nearly impossible journey under powerful wards; lift it in a sealed reliquary and leave at once. Few who try return.

Singular Adamant.hab: At the collapse point at the centre of the Inner Void, a single point of raw adamant; space folds inward there and crushes all who approach.
Singular Adamant.how: Only a worthy master smith can touch it to unfold it into an ingot; the journey takes months and the collapse point kills most who come close.

Unbeing Rose.hab: At the centre of the Inner Void, a rose that exists only when no one is looking; its spot is a blank patch that eyes cannot rest upon.
Unbeing Rose.how: Harvest blindfolded by touch, cutting the stem with silver shears and sealing it in a lightless box; one glance and it vanishes for good.

Firstgrass.hab: Open Primordial plains, where the first grass ever grown covers rolling ground; impossibly green and soft, it grows in thick tufts.
Firstgrass.how: Cut it with a sickle at dawn in an hour or two and tie it in bundles; keep it damp and cool so it stays soft.

Fragment of the Original.hab: Scattered fragments of the first creation lying in Primordial dust and rubble, glinting faintly with a divine spark; commonly found by those who search patiently.
Fragment of the Original.how: Sift loose ground with a fine sieve over a day, picking fragments with bare hands; store them in a small wooden case away from damp.

First Stone.hab: Within the Progenitor Remains, in shallow bedrock laid down when the world began; plain grey stone, unworn by time and very dense.
First Stone.how: Quarry it with ordinary picks and wedges in a day, as it is common there; it is heavy, so haul it out on a cart.

Godmarrow Fungus.hab: Inside the hollow bones of dead gods in the Primordial, golden fungus grows in the marrow cavities; the bones lie half-buried in godfall fields.
Godmarrow Fungus.how: Crack the bone gently with a stone hammer and scrape the fungus into a pouch over an hour; leave some to regrow. Store dry.

Law-ash.hab: Ash drifts in Primordial godfalls, where fallen gods burned and left the laws they held as fine grey ash; the ground hums with order.
Law-ash.how: Scoop it with a brass spoon into sealed jars in an hour or two; keep it dry and do not breathe it, as it binds the breath.

Dawnmetal.hab: Primordial strata laid down before the first sunrise, warm and golden; the seams lie under layers of first rock, a few days' dig deep.
Dawnmetal.how: Mine with ordinary picks over two days; it takes any shape asked of it, so keep it wrapped and still, thinking of nothing.

Primeval Ore.hab: Seams through the Progenitor Remains in the Primordial, laid down in the oldest layers; dark ore runs through the rock like old veins.
Primeval Ore.how: Mine with tempered picks over several days, wearing gloves as it is hot; carry it out in sturdy iron buckets.

Godmarrow Iron.hab: Grown inside the cracked bones of dead gods in the Primordial, where iron fills the marrow; the bones are huge and lie deep in godfall rubble.
Godmarrow Iron.how: Dig to a bone and split it with wedges over days, then pray over the iron before lifting, as it answers prayer. Store in a blessed chest.

Ichor Lily.hab: On the banks of god-blood pools in the Primordial, where divine ichor has spilled; red-gold lilies grow from soil soaked with shining blood.
Ichor Lily.how: Cut the stem with a silver knife and lift it whole, roots wrapped in ichor-soaked moss; the blood burns bare skin, so wear gloves.

Dragonsteel.hab: Hoard-beds of the first dragons in the Primordial, where scale-patterned steel lies in caves warmed like living hides; old dragon guardians may linger.
Dragonsteel.how: Dig through the hoard floor over days under guard, as dragons still come back; smelt it on site in a hot forge and carry ingots out.

Ignis Cinder.hab: Among the remains of Ignis in the Primordial, glowing cinders lie in fields of ash and fire left by the fallen progenitor; heat makes the air shimmer.
Ignis Cinder.how: Walk the ash in fire-warded armour and lift cinders with iron tongs into stone jars; stay only minutes at a time, as the heat is killing.

Sylph Breath.hab: Among the remains of Sylph in the Primordial, where wisps of living wind still drift above high ridges; gusts there whisper and pull at clothing.
Sylph Breath.how: Trap a wisp in a stoppered glass flask held open against the wind, a few hours of waiting; tie yourself down, as gusts can throw one off.

Worldtree Sap.hab: Seeping from the roots of the first tree that held the world together, deep under the Primordial ground; the roots are vast and warm.
Worldtree Sap.how: Descend to the roots over days and tap them with a bronze spout, collecting sap into clay jars; never cut a root, or the ground shakes.

Avatarstone.hab: Golden seams in Primordial depths where ancient beings once walked in borrowed bodies and the Avatar Rune pools; the rock shows faint human outlines.
Avatarstone.how: Cut the whole figure free over several days, keeping its outline intact; wrap it like a person and carry it on a stretcher.

Bathstone.hab: Porous blue seams beneath Primordial springs where the first waters for washing flowed and the Bathe Rune pools; the rock is always damp.
Bathstone.how: Cut it underwater with a bronze chisel over a day, letting the spring flow over it; store it in a wet cloth or a bucket of spring water.

Bleedstone.hab: Crimson seams in Primordial wounds in the earth that never closed, where the Bleed Rune pools; red droplets weep endlessly from the rock.
Bleedstone.how: Cut it with a clean blade over a day and catch its droplets in a bowl; store in a sealed clay jar lined with cloth.

Breakstone.hab: Shattered seams in Primordial fields where nothing stays whole and the Break Rune pools; the stone breaks and reassembles from its own fragments.
Breakstone.how: Gather every fragment into a sack before it reforms, as one missed piece leaves it incomplete; a half day's careful work.

Converge Stone.hab: Under Primordial plains where every road leads to a single point and the Converge Rune pools; lines in the rock all point inward.
Converge Stone.how: Dig at the exact point where the roads meet, over two days; lift it whole and store it in a round box.

Demonstone.hab: Vast swarming beds of red-black stone in the Primordial where the Demon Rune pools; the stone crawls and whispers in many small voices.
Demonstone.how: Cut it in teams with plugs in your ears to block the whispers; seal each piece in a warded iron box at once. Several days.

Dirtystone.hab: Grimy seams beneath filthy Primordial mires where the Dirty Rune pools; slime coats everything and never washes off.
Dirtystone.how: Dig in disposable clothing and burn it after; store the stone in sealed clay jars, as its slime stains all it touches.

Eurus Stone.hab: Green-blue seams in Primordial storm cliffs where the Eurus Rune pools; an eastern wind sighs from the rock and plants grow fast nearby.
Eurus Stone.how: Climb the cliff on calm days, tied fast, and cut it with a chisel over a day; store in a sealed box to quiet its wind.

Fusionstone.hab: In the deepest Primordial seams where laws first merged and the Fusion Rune pools; colours melt into one another and never settle.
Fusionstone.how: Reach the deep seams over weeks and cut with care, as touching pieces merge; keep cut parts apart in separate cases.

Glaivestone.hab: Long silver-grey seams in Primordial cliffs of ancient metal where the Glaive Rune pools, shaped like a blade on a staff and keen along one edge.
Glaivestone.how: Cut it out along its length in heavy gauntlets over two days; lower it from the cliff on ropes and sheathe its edge.

Kistone.hab: Clear seams deep in Primordial mountains of power where the Ki Rune pools; a breathing gold-white glow pulses inside the rock.
Kistone.how: Meditate at the seam before cutting, as it answers calm; mine slowly over days and store it in an open, airy box.

Metalstone.hab: Molten-silver seams in the Primordial depths where the Metal Rune pools; the stone ripples when touched and rings like a bell.
Metalstone.how: Scoop it into a ceramic crucible with a ladle, as it never fully settles; carry it slowly in heat-proof gloves.

Potentialstone.hab: Plain smooth seams in the Primordial where the Potential Rune pools, humming with untapped energy; its full shape never shows.
Potentialstone.how: Cut a rough block around it over days with plain tools, as its edges hide; store in a padded crate and expect surprises.

Progenitor Ginseng.hab: Growing in Primordial progenitor graves, where roots shaped like sleeping progenitors pulse like heartbeats in the deep soil.
Progenitor Ginseng.how: Dig around the root with bare hands over a day, never cutting it; wrap it in damp moss and pay respects to the grave.

Ringstone.hab: Pale stone circles in Primordial depths where the Ring Rune pools, orbiting other laws like a planet's halo; they circle slowly in the rock.
Ringstone.how: Wait until it passes close and slip a rod through its centre to catch it; store it hanging on a peg.

Shorterstone.hab: Tiny dense stones in Primordial depths where length shrinks to nothing and the Shorter Rune pools; distances seem shorter near it.
Shorterstone.how: Do not measure it; pick it up quickly with fine tweezers and store it in a tiny box, or it shrinks out of sight.

Slothstone.hab: Heavy grey stones in Primordial hollows where nothing has moved since the first age and the Sloth Rune pools; the will to work drains there.
Slothstone.how: Use winches and pulleys rather than muscle, as it saps the will to lift; work in short shifts and haul it on a cart.

Takestone.hab: Hungry violet seams in the oldest grasping deeps of the Primordial where the Take Rune pools; hooked ridges pull at nearby objects.
Takestone.how: Mine with tools tied to your belt, as it grabs loose items; store in a locked box and count your belongings after.

Wastestone.hab: Brittle ashen seams in dead, barren stretches of the Primordial where the Waste Rune pools; nothing grows and the ground is grey.
Wastestone.how: Lift it gently with cupped hands into a padded jar, as gripping crumbles it; a slow half day's work.

Elderwyrm Pepper.hab: Growing in Primordial progenitor dragon hoards, among gold and bones; red-black peppers sprout from cracks hot with old dragon breath.
Elderwyrm Pepper.how: Pick it in fire-warded gloves and seal it in clay jars, as it burns like dragon fire; old dragons may still guard the hoard.

Genesis Crystal.hab: In the deepest Primordial remains, where creation first began; clear crystals glow with divine light in caverns no one has reached in ages.
Genesis Crystal.how: Reach the deep remains after weeks of travel and cut with blessed tools; store in a golden reliquary and guard it well.

Progenitor Gold.hab: Veins in the bodies of the progenitors in the Primordial, where gold runs like blood through the remains; life sprouts around it.
Progenitor Gold.how: Mine with respect over days, never wasting any; store in a sealed chest, as it makes everything nearby more alive.

Genesis Seed.hab: Buried at the world's foundation in the Primordial, a seed from before creation holding a whole forest inside; it lies far below all else.
Genesis Seed.how: Reach the foundation after months of descent and lift it with cupped hands; store it in a sealed, earth-filled box, never letting it touch soil.

Heart Shard of an Original God.hab: Inside an original god's corpse in the Primordial, deep in its vast body; the shard beats faintly and is guarded by the god's lingering power.
Heart Shard of an Original God.how: Reach the corpse after an epic quest and cut the shard free with divine tools; store in a blessed reliquary. Many die trying.

Raw Adamant.hab: In the bones of creation at the Primordial's foundation, where unworked adamant forms the hardest substance that exists; almost no one can reach it.
Raw Adamant.how: Only adamant tools can cut it, and the work takes months at crushing depth; carry it out in reinforced crates. Few survive.

Wardleaf.hab: Low shrubs beside old shrines and in churchyards, where generations of prayers have soaked into the soil.
Wardleaf.how: Pick the leaves at dawn while they are still curled, and press them flat between cloth. Fold into charms or stitch into a lining while fresh.

Ironheart Ore.hab: Deep seams in old hill mines, as red-black nodules in grey rock that feel warm to the touch.
Ironheart Ore.how: Pick the nodules out whole with a light hammer and chisel; smelt hot in a bellows furnace. One sack of nodules gives a few ingots.

Clearwater Lotus.hab: The still centres of cold mountain tarns, where the water is so clear the bottom looks close enough to touch.
Clearwater Lotus.how: Wade or swim out and cut the stem below the water line. Keep the flower floating in a bowl of the same water until it is worked.

Wardsilver.hab: Thin veins under ruined temples, often found where the rock has been blackened by an old curse.
Wardsilver.how: Mine slowly and test each chunk with a drop of holy water: wardsilver beads it. Smelt with charcoal from a shrine fire.

Cinderwake Moss.hab: Patches on cooling lava fields in Hell, glowing faintly wherever something has walked past.
Cinderwake Moss.how: Scrape it into a lidded iron tin with a long spatula. It smoulders when disturbed, so pack it with ash.

Oathiron.hab: The bedrock under the devils' contract halls, in seams stamped with old signatures.
Oathiron.how: Mining it needs permission from whoever holds the hall, or a very quiet night. Smelt in a hellfire forge; it will not melt in an ordinary one.

Haloward Lily.hab: Cloud meadows in Heaven, growing in rings around places where angels once stood.
Haloward Lily.how: Lift the whole bulb with a silver trowel so the ring of light stays whole. Replant or work it within a day.

Serene Electrum.hab: Seams under the choir terraces of Heaven, recognised by the faint single note they hum.
Serene Electrum.how: Cut it out with a fine pick while the choir is singing, which keeps the metal calm. Refine in a temple forge.

Flickerfern.hab: Groves in Chaos that shift from day to day; the fern is never in the same place twice.
Flickerfern.how: Mark it with chalk the moment you see it, then cut it quickly. Store it in a lead box so it stays put.

Stillpoint Ore.hab: The calm centres of chaos storms, where the ground stops changing for a little while.
Stillpoint Ore.how: Wait for a storm's eye to pass over a seam, then dig fast before it moves on. Smelts like ordinary iron.

Deepcalm Kelp.hab: Silent trenches in the Abyss where the demons' whispers do not reach.
Deepcalm Kelp.how: Dive or drop a hooked line, cut the fronds, and dry them in the dark. Keep them away from loud noise.

Bulwark Pyrite.hab: The rubble of collapsed demon forts, in heavy golden chunks that survived what crushed the walls.
Bulwark Pyrite.how: Dig through the rubble and sort the chunks by weight. Work it cold: heat makes it brittle.

Lawward Clover.hab: The ordered gardens of the Inner Realm, always in perfect rows.
Lawward Clover.how: Count the leaves before picking: only the four-leafed ones carry the ward. Dry flat in a book of law.

Truthglass Ore.hab: The foundations of courthouses and oath-stones in the Inner Realm.
Truthglass Ore.how: Cut it out in clear blocks; lies spoken nearby cloud it, so work in silence. Grind and fuse into glass or metal.

Farsight Sage.hab: High star-plains in the Outer Realm, on the slopes that face the most stars.
Farsight Sage.how: Cut the stems at night and hang them to dry under the open sky. Burn or weave the dried leaves.

Starward Iron.hab: Craters where stars have fallen in the Outer Realm, in pitted grey-black lumps.
Starward Iron.how: Dig out the meteorite whole and cut it with a diamond-edged saw. Smelt only in a forge cooled by night air.

Quietroot.hab: Soundless hollows in the Void, where no echo comes back.
Quietroot.how: Dig without speaking; any sound makes the root wither. Wrap it in wool until it is used.

Nullward Slag.hab: Heaps outside abandoned null forges at the edges of the Void.
Nullward Slag.how: Shovel the slag into sacks and remelt it in a Void forge. Ordinary flame does not touch it.

Unshaken Lichen.hab: The oldest stones in the Inner Void, older than the realms.
Unshaken Lichen.how: Scrape it off with a bone knife and keep it on a piece of the same stone, or it crumbles.

Edgewake Ore.hab: The rim of the Inner Void, in seams that hum louder as anyone approaches.
Edgewake Ore.how: Approach slowly so the seam does not crack from its own humming; cut and quench in cold water.

First-Ward Seed.hab: The first gardens of the Primordial realm, beneath the oldest guardian trees.
First-Ward Seed.how: Collect fallen seeds by hand from the roots. Plant one, or crush and bind it into a ward with resin.

Worldspine Ore.hab: The exposed spine of the world in the Primordial realm, where the bedrock rises in ridges.
Worldspine Ore.how: Only a Realm Forge can melt it. Cut slabs with tools of Primordial metal, and expect it to take a full tenday.

Owl-Eye Agate.hab: River gravel beds in the Human Realm.
Owl-Eye Agate.how: Mine it with a pick and smelt or cut it in a forge fit for its realm; work it soon after it is taken.

Honeytongue Clover.how: Cut it by hand, wrap it in cloth, and dry or press it within a day.
